docs/A2A.md:
# A2A agents over the durable queue

The running application exposes two real A2A 1.0 JSON-RPC servers using the
official Python SDK 1.3.0. Each publishes a discoverable Agent Card:

| Agent | Card on localhost:8010 | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dispatcher | `/a2a/dispatcher/.well-known/agent-card.json` | Dispatch pending Madrid-baseline orders with the existing road/energy/shift policy. |
| Customer service | `/a2a/customer_service/.well-known/agent-card.json` | Classify an existing complaint with the scripted Google ADK model and enforce the existing refund approval policy. |

The request is a text part containing JSON with `run_id` and `entity_id`. An
entity must already exist in that run. The adapter publishes (or reuses) the
canonical durable event, claims a fenced lease, and invokes the existing role
handler. It processes at most 32 eligible events per request. Concurrent work or
backoff can return a `ready` or `leased` queue state; only `done` means the event
has committed. An assigned delivery still requires the simulation clock to
advance its courier. The adapter does not fabricate physical completion.

```bash
make setup
curl http://localhost:8010/a2a/dispatcher/.well-known/agent-card.json
python3 scripts/call_a2a.py dispatcher RUN_UUID ORDER_ID
python3 scripts/call_a2a.py customer_service RUN_UUID COMPLAINT_ID
```

Use identifiers from `/api/state` or a seeded baseline run. These endpoints wrap
the Madrid-baseline dispatcher and customer service, not the separate inventory
lab's scoped fleet. The client uses `A2ACardResolver`, `ClientFactory`, and
`SendMessageRequest`, including protocol version negotiation. Raw JSON-RPC
clients must send `A2A-Version: 1.0`. A response contains the queue event ID,
attempt count, domain outcome, and `paid_calls_this_request: 0`.

Customer inference is explicitly pinned to the offline ADK adapter even if the
host has a paid provider configured. Scripted advice uses `adk_offline`, so the
existing refund gate asks for human approval and never grants a refund based on
fixture output. Repeating an entity request reuses its event and cached model
receipt; it does not reserve a second inference call. No model or SQL tool calls
are accepted from a client.

This is a local demonstration: Compose binds port 8010 to loopback; the adapter
also checks Host/Origin and caps the streamed HTTP body at 8 KiB. The immediate
A2A Message workflow is advertised without streaming or push notifications.
Business work survives process restarts in PostgreSQL; no durable A2A task store
is claimed. An internet deployment requires authentication, tenant-to-run
authorization, ingress limits, and a reviewed public Agent Card.

Implementation: [server and queue adapter](../src/delivery/a2a_server.py),
[SDK client](../scripts/call_a2a.py), and
[protocol plus real-agent integration tests](../tests/test_a2a_server.py).
Tests discover both cards and call both servers using the real SDK over ASGI;
the integration case checks actual courier assignment, ADK advice, refund
escalation, and replay with one durable zero-dollar reservation.

Official references checked on 2026-10-29:
[A2A Python SDK](https://a2aproject.github.io/a2a-python/) and
[server tutorial](https://a2a-protocol.org/latest/tutorials/python/5-start-server/).
The installed 1.3 SDK uses protobuf message types; pre-1.0 Pydantic examples
are not used here.
docs/ADK-RESTAURANT.md:
# Google ADK restaurant agent

This slice uses **Google ADK 2.13.0** and its real `LlmAgent`, `Runner`, function
tools, model callbacks and session service. The default model is explicitly a
scripted offline `BaseLlm` double. A native Vertex/Gemini adapter is implemented
behind an explicit deployment gate and monetary budget; it is disabled by default
and was exercised explicitly with both SOULs on Vertex on 2026-10-29. There is no automatic
paid-provider fallback. Offline results demonstrate integration
and enforcement; they do not measure a language model's understanding of SOUL.

## Reusable building blocks

Source map: [template contract](../src/delivery/adk_contracts.py),
[ADK turn and tools](../src/delivery/adk_restaurant.py),
[native model adapter](../src/delivery/adk_models.py),
[offline model double](../src/delivery/adk_offline.py),
[scoped turn/transaction SQL](../sql/migrations/017_adk_restaurant.sql),
[Vertex admission SQL](../sql/migrations/018_adk_vertex_admission.sql), and
[executable checks](../tests/test_adk_restaurant.py).
The editable [role prompt](../config/agents/restaurant-adk/PROMPT.md),
[speed SOUL](../config/agents/restaurant-adk/SOUL-speed.md) and
[cost SOUL](../config/agents/restaurant-adk/SOUL-cost.md) are resolved into the
frozen restaurant definition.

`RestaurantBrain` is the validated template contract. A restaurant instance
combines that contract with its existing entity, authenticated database identity,
role limits, role prompt and SOUL. The operator can edit the prompt/SOUL and bounded
budgets in `/restaurant-lab`, through its revision-checked blueprint endpoint, or
in advanced agent JSON. Choose **Override for this entity** or **Edit shared role
template**, then **Google ADK · offline model fixture**. The two Load profile
prompts options initialize Elena (shortest quoted lead time) and Mateo (lowest
quoted procurement fee). Saving a blueprint affects new runs, never an existing
agent's frozen definition.

`config/agents/restaurant-adk/PROMPT.md` supplies the reusable role prompt;
`SOUL-speed.md` and `SOUL-cost.md` supply the initial profiles. The template endpoint
`GET /api/supply/agent-templates` exposes resolved, approved local templates. No
configuration field names an executable module, arbitrary URL or credential.
Tool references can remove supported capabilities; extending authority requires
reviewed code, permissions and tests. A template cannot grant another role's tools.

Effective instructions combine a fixed platform boundary, the editable role prompt
and editable SOUL. A callable instruction provider preserves literal braces in
operator text. ADK initially receives only the leased event identifier; the actual
order and event facts come from scoped SQL tools. Forged caller-side event bodies
cannot enter model context or select a different order. Every turn gets a fresh, private
in-memory ADK session. Cross-event working memory comes from the existing typed
Postgres recall functions; broad session history is not shared between agents.

## Granular tools

| ADK function | Capability | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `read_order` | `restaurant.order` | Current order, event, deadline and canonical alternative |
| `read_pantry` | `restaurant.pantry` | This kitchen's physical stock and reservations |
| `read_recipe` | `restaurant.recipe` | This meal's frozen recipe and units |
| `find_suppliers` | `restaurant.suppliers` | Open markets' public fees and estimated lead times; no private stock |
| `recall_order_memory` | `memory.read` | Current-order, restaurant-owned, unexpired typed observations |
| `search_ingredients` | `supply.search` (optional) | Scoped ingredient relevance; separate local/Jev provider and budget |
| `request_missing_ingredients` | `restaurant.request_supply` | Stage a supplier choice; SQL calculates shortages and queues requests |
| `confirm_order` | `restaurant.confirm` | Stage pantry-only acceptance; a shortage invalidates the proposal |
| `receive_ingredient` | `restaurant.receive` | Stage receipt of the ingredient addressed by this event |
| `prepare_meal` | `restaurant.cook` | Stage cooking after arrival, consent and timing checks |
| `offer_substitution` | `restaurant.offer` | Stage the safe alternative; queue the household's approval request |
| `decline_order` | `restaurant.decline` | Stage a bounded reason and reservation release |
| `finish_decision` | `restaurant.finish` | Seal one staged action with a brief explanation |

The model chooses which tools to use and which supplier/action to propose. The
shared runtime does not choose the sourcing strategy. The offline model double
implements the two documented fixture strategies to exercise that interface;
it should be replaced with an evaluated generative model for intelligence tests.

Quotes are synthetic entity settings. `procurement_fee_cents` is editable entity
data. Lead time is an estimate derived from grid distance and supplier delay,
not a guaranteed route ETA or stock promise. Supermarket workers continue using
their deterministic policy and reply only through queued messages.

## Transaction and recovery boundaries

1. Claim the addressed event and commit its ordinary tool/event budget ticket.
2. Begin a durable restaurant turn containing the frozen definition hash, canonical
   event payload and scoped business snapshot. A nonce fences the original owner.
3. Before **each** ADK model call, save a request hash and conservative token
   reservation. Close the SQL connection before model execution. Save the model
   completion receipt separately. No provider/model retries are automatic.
4. Read tools each use a short authenticated transaction and retain a receipt.
   Write tools only stage a proposal; they make no stock changes or agent calls.
5. Save the completed plan durably. The final effects transaction rechecks the
   current business snapshot, recalled memory versions/expiry, event/action pair,
   permitted tool receipts and live lease. SQL computes physical quantities and
   enforces supplier validity, exclusions, consent, reservations and cooking.
6. Commit domain effects, queue outbox, replay facts, typed outcome memory,
   decision receipt, applied marker and event ACK together.

A saved completed plan can be consumed after lease reclamation without repeating
ADK calls. Death during an unfinished turn marks it unknown on reclamation and
fails closed; it does not regenerate a partially completed decision. Changed
business observations or expired/revised recalled facts invalidate a saved plan.
Such turns need explicit operator handling. This chooses bounded retries and
auditability over automatic availability; external exactly-once billing is not claimed.

## Authorization and budgets

ADK restaurants use their own `lab_restaurant_adk_executor` PostgreSQL group, not
the legacy supply executor. It has no stock, memory-history, turn-table or broad
`supply_context`/`supply_command` grants. All granular functions reconstruct scope
from `session_user`, a live addressed lease and a durable budget ticket. The model
cannot supply a run, order, namespace or agent identity in tool arguments. ADK's
tool callback also rejects unknown fields/types before execution.

The existing event/tool/memory limits remain independent of instructions. New
brain limits cap model calls per event and per restaurant/run, serialized token
reservations, request bytes, output tokens and wall time. A run-wide ceiling also
limits aggregate restaurant calls/tokens. Reservations survive failures and are
not refunded. Bytes of the serialized text-only request conservatively reserve
input tokens; configured output allowance is reserved too. This is not a tokenizer
or a measurement of actual Gemini usage. Offline inference has zero provider
cost. Native Vertex admission additionally reserves money at the frozen approved
input/output rates, rounds upward and checks the restaurant's `usd_limit` plus a
$10 run-wide reservation ceiling. The unpriced admission helper is private.
Reservations survive timeouts and crashes, with no automatic refund. These limits
bound admitted work at configured rates; they do not enforce a billing-account
cap or compensate for a provider tariff change. Unknown actual billing stays unknown.
ADK model limits live in `brain`; the legacy `RoleLimits` model fields retain the
older judge contract. Operator inspection shows the separate ADK reservation
counters rather than treating those legacy zero fields as actual ADK usage.

The trusted local host/controller remains outside this isolation boundary. This
is not an OS sandbox for arbitrary agent code. Inspection endpoints are trusted
operator views and are not registered ADK tools.

## Optional native Vertex model adapter

`adk_models.py` constructs ADK's `Gemini` with Vertex enabled, a specific approved
project/region/model, stable API version `v1`, ADC credentials and one HTTP attempt.
It never accepts an API key or arbitrary model endpoint from a prompt/blueprint.
A Vertex brain requires a positive `usd_limit` and a `vertex` profile containing
`project`, `location`, `model`, `input_usd_per_million` and `output_usd_per_million`.
The trusted deployment must separately set `DELIVERY_ADK_VERTEX_ENABLED=1` and
`DELIVERY_ADK_VERTEX_PROFILE` to that exact approved JSON profile. Missing approval,
different project/model/pricing, unapproved adapters or exhausted budgets fail closed.
The normal UI loads only offline profiles; configuring Vertex requires an operator
to prepare the advanced definition and deployment policy explicitly.

No credentials are discovered until an approved native model is actually invoked.
The local Compose defaults contain no ADC mount. In a GCP workload, ADC should
come from its least-privilege runtime identity. Test profile prices and project IDs
are fictional inputs, not recommended Google prices. Model availability, region,
current tariffs and IAM are operator deployment choices. The explicit live comparison
below exercises this adapter without enabling paid execution in the normal city UI.

## Verification and GCP direction

Run the reproducible offline checks with the local Postgres services available:

```bash
make test-adk
```

`make demo-adk` retains two one-order runs for inspecting the profiles in the UI
and writes `artifacts/adk-restaurants-demo.json`. It changes no saved blueprint,
uses only this project's local database, and never selects Vertex. Default city
demand is much larger than this bounded comparison; model/tool budgets still
stop an over-budget ADK worker rather than silently enabling an unbounded run.

Tests use only `delivery_test`, restricted identities, real ADK function calls and
an HTTP-blocking fixture. They cover both profiles through sourcing and physical
delivery, replay, prompts reaching ADK, foreign roles/runs, raw-table/legacy denial,
budgets, stale stock, invalid suppliers, unfinished-turn rejection and saved-plan
recovery. A worker is also terminated as a real process after saving its plan.
The health dashboard lists these cases under **ADK restaurant agents**.

Google-native components implemented here are ADK, Google Gen AI types and a gated
keyless Vertex model adapter. The
existing isolated Terraform Cloud Run/Vertex recovery judge is separate. The
local city and Postgres remain free local infrastructure. Production work still
includes billing reconciliation, broader model-quality evaluation and a supervised worker.
Cloud Run or managed-runtime hosting must be Terraform-owned before deployment;
ADK names or sessions do not create IAM identities. No new GCP resource is required
or provisioned by the offline checks.

## Historical Vertex and Jev comparison

The native restaurant worker stays local and impersonates a dedicated, keyless
`restaurant-adk` service account in the isolated simulation project. Terraform
owns the identity, its `aiplatform.endpoints.predict` grant and the permitted
operator impersonation binding. This mode enables the project's billing link
without creating Cloud Run, Artifact Registry, Cloud SQL or a managed agent runtime.
The existing judge gateway is not deployed for these tests. Project, APIs and IAM
remain when billing is parked.

```bash
make gcp-vertex-start
make demo-adk-vertex
make gcp-stop
make gcp-status
```

Each SOUL gets one synthetic pizza order, an empty pantry and three public
supplier quotes. Elena should prioritize lead time; Mateo should prioritize
procurement fee. Both use the same ADK tool implementation. Gemini decides the
tool sequence and supplier from the prompt and SOUL; the SQL layer validates
authority, quantities, consent and event effects. No paid model selects the stock
quantities or bypasses the queue.

The reviewed model is `gemini-3.5-flash-lite`, global, standard text PayGo:
$0.30 / million input tokens, $2.50 / million output tokens including thinking,
and $0.03 / million cached input tokens, checked 2026-10-29. Gemini 3 uses minimal
thinking for this bounded trial. Global is deliberate for synthetic data and
does not assert EU processing residency. The retired 2.5 model is not used.

Jev `jev-1.14.0` is an optional `supply.search` capability, not a general planner.
The model may call `search_ingredients` with a canonical ingredient ID from the
current recipe. The server selects the already scoped restaurant index and
frozen review provider. Jev receives ingredient labels, units and a relevance
question; it receives no inventory counts, household conversations or typed memory.
Its result is an observation. Availability is read again locally; reservation
and supplier communication still require the transactional tools and event queue.
Its input-only tariff is $0.042 / million tokens, output free. An API key is held
in ignored `.env.jev` and passed only to the one-shot worker.

The comparison admits at most $0.20 Vertex work per SOUL ($0.40 together),
60 calls per agent, eight per event, 1,024 output tokens per call, and a 30-second
event deadline. Each agent also gets three Jev calls and 24,000 reserved input
tokens: together $0.002016 maximum at the reviewed Jev tariff. No automatic
provider retries, provider fallback or fresh paid experiments follow a failure.
An exclusive execution lock prevents concurrent launches. Explicit receipt recovery
can re-read finished runs without repeating calls; reviewed follow-up experiments
account for previous known costs, reserving the full allowance for unknown calls,
against a cumulative $0.50 Vertex limit. Operator-controlled local files and
SQL admission are not a billing-account spending cap.

The retained live comparison delivered both meals, with 25 Gemini calls and three
Jev calls per SOUL. Elena selected `market-a` (90-second quoted lead time); Mateo
selected `market-b` (50-cent fee). Both runs acknowledged 24 events, had zero
retries/dead letters, conserved stock and replayed correctly. Median Gemini call
latency was 800 ms for Elena and 769 ms for Mateo. Their Vertex costs calculated
from actual usage were $0.01214980 and $0.01269700; Jev was $0.000136962 each.
Including the initial trial, total usage-derived cost was $0.039755624. Billing
was then disabled, retaining 15 foundation resources. A live impersonated IAM
probe received HTTP 403 / PERMISSION_DENIED for `resourcemanager.projects.get`.

These two synthetic orders prove integration and the intended SOUL distinction;
they are not a general model-quality benchmark or proof of cost/latency savings
from a Jev cascade. That baseline invokes Gemini on routine arrival and cooking
events. The Jev-first implementation below compares that baseline with selective
escalation on the same scenarios.
One recovered receipt has no whole-run wall time; per-call latency and token
metadata were durably retained and remain available.

[AI evidence](/agent-traces) shows the retained comparison, system prompts and
SOULs, tool declarations, model-visible messages, function calls, tool results,
selected memory with provenance/expiry/version, provider model version, latency,
tokens and usage-derived costs. Full private rows are not granted to agents.
The page never starts inference. Costs calculated from actual token metadata are
separate from invoice totals, credits, tax and project-wide charges; missing
metadata remains unknown. Previous attempts remain in the local JSON receipt.

Source links: [operator evidence reader](../src/delivery/adk_evidence.py),
[paid comparison](../scripts/demo_adk_vertex.py),
[temporary impersonated ADC launcher](../scripts/run_adk_vertex.py),
[model trace schema](../sql/migrations/019_adk_model_traces.sql),
[scoped search grants](../sql/migrations/020_adk_scoped_search.sql),
[canonical business snapshots](../sql/migrations/021_canonical_supply_context.sql),
and [usage-cost and operator-boundary tests](../tests/test_adk_evidence.py).

An initial real run exposed unordered JSON inventory arrays: equal stock facts
could fail stale-state validation after a different query plan. Canonical ordering
fixes that comparison while preserving version/quantity checks. A regression test
rewrites physical stock rows without changing their business values; existing
stale-stock tests continue to reject actual changes.

## Jev-first decisions and bounded model selection

Set `brain.routing.strategy` to `jev_first` in an ADK restaurant definition. The
operator editor exposes the routing strategy, confidence and margin; advanced JSON
also controls the pinned Jev model, router instructions, calls, tokens and money.
Leaving routing unset preserves the existing ADK model tool loop. These settings
are frozen with the agent at run creation; editing a template cannot change a live run.

The execution path is:

1. Physical ingredient-arrival and cooking events follow their single validated
   protocol action without a model. This does not choose suppliers or substitutions.
2. For an order, approval or shortage judgment, the worker retrieves only this
   restaurant's current recipe, required pantry rows, public supplier quotes and
   selected current-order memory. Household identity, raw call transcript, other
   orders and supermarket stock are omitted from Jev's request.
3. One Jev request classifies requested work (finite action/factual receipt versus
   explicit reasoning), the permitted action, and, when sourcing is needed, a
   quoted supplier versus abstention. A stocked-pantry call omits both the supplier
   lookup and its irrelevant question. The editable role prompt and SOUL remain
   inputs. Jev cannot invent tool names, models or URLs.
4. Direct action requires confidence at least **0.85**, top-to-second probability
   margin at least **0.20** on every relevant question, valid response shape and
   locally supported evidence. Stock sufficiency, replacement consent and tool
   authority remain mandatory. These thresholds are configurable starting values,
   not a calibrated guarantee of correctness on this domain.
5. Jev's request for reasoning, low certainty, unsupported action or an invalid/
   missing provider response permits the separately budgeted Gemini tool loop.
   An exhausted router budget or missing deployment permission fails closed.
6. Both paths stage the same typed plan through the same granular tools. SQL
   validates and commits effects, memory, outbox and ACK atomically. Jev never
   contacts a supermarket directly or changes stock.

The approved executor registry currently contains **no further model** and the
frozen Gemini Vertex profile. Jev chooses whether that model is needed; it does
not gain permission to choose a more expensive model, provider, region or identity.
Adding another approved tier requires a reviewed adapter, deployment allowlist,
tariff and eval cases. This keeps model selection editable within an explicit
security and cost boundary.

Before dispatch, Postgres stores the Jev request and reserves input bytes plus
2,048 tokens at the pinned input tariff. A single durable router receipt is allowed
per event. The result, probabilities, confidence, margin, executor, reason, known
usage and latency are saved before downstream Gemini admission or effects. Network
calls run outside transactions. Unknown usage keeps the full reservation. No
provider retry or automatic resumption repeats a pending request after a crash.
The ordinary saved-plan recovery path remains available after a complete result.

This is currently a **restaurant** decision adapter. Other roles share selectable
memory and enforcement but retain their existing deterministic or judge policy;
they are not silently converted to autonomous Jev agents.

Run the bounded matched comparison explicitly:

```bash
make gcp-vertex-start
make demo-adk-routing
make gcp-stop
make gcp-status
```

It executes one order each for speed, cost and an explicitly requested fast-versus-
cheap explanation, in baseline and cascade mode: six runs. Each pair uses the same
SOUL, city seed, demand and typed memory. Baseline retains the prior initial Jev
mozzarella relevance search; cascade uses Jev for decisions and optional relevance
search only after Gemini escalation. This compares the two complete configurations,
not an isolated causal effect of one provider. The combined admission allowance is
$0.54 Vertex plus less than $0.01 Jev, within $0.60. The permanent experiment marker
prevents repeat spending, even if its UI receipt is lost. The normal UI has no keys,
ADC mount or paid deployment gate.

[AI evidence](/agent-traces) exposes each arm's outcomes, provider counts, costs,
wall time and routing decisions. A cost saving is reported only for a pair with
matched supplier choice, delivery, queue, replay, stock and complete known usage.
Provider medians have different call mixes; baseline legacy Jev search latency is
an aggregate operation and is excluded from provider p50. One order per arm is a
smoke comparison, not a statistically established quality or speed improvement.

### Live routing result: 2026-10-29

The complete six-arm comparison **failed its outcome gate**, with four meals
delivered. The failure remains visible in `/agent-traces`; this is not a release
approval for making the cascade the default.

| SOUL | Baseline Gemini calls / cost / wall time | Jev-first Gemini calls / cost / wall time | Outcome |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Speed | 23 / 0.011208962 USD / 37.634 s | 7 / 0.002920592 USD / 11.845 s | Both delivered; same supplier, conserved stock and matching replay |
| Cost | 25 / 0.012906462 USD / 32.460 s | 6 / 0.002402218 USD / 10.369 s | Cascade rejected an invented `finish_finish_decision` tool; no applied sourcing effects |
| Explain trade-off | 23 / 0.012891262 USD / 31.913 s | 6 / 0.002820798 USD / 12.448 s | Jev explicitly chose Gemini; its 574-character finish summary exceeded the 500-character contract |

Costs include actual reported Vertex and Jev usage at the frozen tariffs. The
failed runs' lower costs do not support a savings claim. Only the speed pair
matched outcomes: its observed cost fell by 73.9% and wall time by 68.5%. These
changes combine five no-model protocol events, Jev routing and less relevance
searching; they cannot be attributed to Jev alone.

All three live judgments escalated: speed confidence was 0.68, cost 0.56, and
reasoning 0.84 with an explicit Gemini choice. The 0.85 direct-action threshold
was not lowered after observing results. Direct Jev actions were verified with
injected responses locally, **not established by these live trials**. Jev router
latency was 208, 162 and 157 ms respectively. The provider-mix median in the
operator table includes downstream Gemini calls and is a different measurement.

After the cost failure, the original attempt stopped. A reviewed, one-time
continuation dispatched only the two untouched reasoning plans, under the same
six original configurations and cumulative ceilings. It did not retry a failed
event, replace a run, reset a budget or overwrite earlier evidence. Hashes of the
four preserved arms were checked before and after continuation. The second failure
stopped that continuation; all six planned arms had then been attempted.

Total known usage was **0.045150294 USD**, with **0.460544866 USD** conservatively
accounted using reservations for admitted work, below the 0.60 USD ceiling. No
usage was unknown. Invoice reconciliation remains pending. The retained summary
is `docs/evidence/jev-routing-comparison.json`; full local model/tool receipts
remain in `artifacts/adk-route-comparison.json`.

The next quality gate is stronger model-visible tool constraints and bounded
handling of malformed proposals, followed by a new, explicitly budgeted evaluation.
Scope, consent, stock validation and summary limits must remain enforced. The
existing failed examples must remain in the evaluation set; repeatedly rerunning
until a green sample appears would conceal the failure rate.

Sources: [Jev decision adapter](../src/delivery/jev_routing.py),
[router admission and result schema](../sql/migrations/022_jev_decision_routing.sql),
[local failure/isolation checks](../tests/test_jev_routing.py),
[matched comparison runner](../scripts/compare_agent_routing.py).

## Tool-contract enforcement and correction

Gemini requests now use `VALIDATED` function calling with an explicit allowlist
derived from this frozen agent's actual tools. The platform instructions, role
prompt and `finish_decision` declaration state the 1–500-character summary limit.
Google's function schema support does not make arbitrary string-length constraints
a server guarantee; Python and SQL continue to enforce the bound independently.

A completed model proposal can receive a structured `tool_contract` response for
an invented function name or an invalid summary length. An invented name is never
aliased or executed. A long summary is never silently truncated. The agent must
propose an exact declared function or rewrite its explanation while keeping its
original staged action. Successful `finish_decision` ends the ADK loop, avoiding
a further model call just to summarize the saved decision.

Postgres records each rejection in the existing private tool-receipt ledger,
under the current authenticated turn, nonce and lease. At most two corrections
are allowed per event, serialized with the live turn lock. Each costs an ordinary
tool slot, and each subsequent model call needs its own durable token/money
admission. The correction helper requires a completed model response and refuses
unfinished dispatches, finished plans and foreign roles. Scope-bearing arguments,
disabled tools, budget denials, stale facts and lease failures remain fatal. No
provider timeout or unknown dispatch is retried by this mechanism.

Local tests replay both observed failures, verify one staging receipt and one
valid finish before atomic effects, and terminate repeated malformed proposals
without sourcing. Cross-role helper calls and scope injection remain denied.

The one-shot live verification is separate from the original failed comparison:

```bash
make gcp-vertex-start
make verify-adk-contracts
make gcp-stop
```

It runs three one-order cases: a stocked pantry for direct Jev confirmation,
Mateo's cost explanation and Elena's speed-versus-fee explanation. The latter
cases explicitly request reasoned explanations to exercise Gemini's tool contract.
They are repair checks, not a new paired architecture benchmark. Thresholds remain
0.85 confidence and 0.20 margin. Each case admits one Jev call and no legacy
relevance searches; Vertex admission is at most 0.06 USD in each Gemini case.
The combined conservative reservation ceiling is 0.1215 USD, within a 0.15 USD
allowance. A permanent marker prevents automatic repeat spending.

The direct case uses an offline secondary-model profile with a one-token
admission ceiling. If Jev is uncertain, it cannot dispatch any secondary model.
Success requires an actual validated Jev `direct` / `confirm` response, physical
delivery, and an empty model-call ledger—not merely zero Gemini cost. All cases
must preserve stock, replay and queue invariants and deny raw stock/model/router
table access through the restaurant's actual login. The normal UI retains no
provider credentials or paid opt-in. `/agent-traces` shows the new results above
the unchanged failed comparison.

Sources: [correction admission and receipt function](../sql/migrations/025_adk_contract_corrections.sql),
[bounded live verifier](../scripts/verify_adk_contracts.py).
Official references: [Google function-calling modes](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/tools/function-calling),
[ADK tool callback responses](https://adk.dev/callbacks/types-of-callbacks/).

### Repair verification: 2026-10-29

All three new cases passed with real Jev and Vertex. The earlier failed six-arm
comparison remains unchanged and visible below this verification in the UI.

| Case | Jev / Gemini calls | Known token cost | Router latency / run wall time | Outcome |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Iris, stocked pantry | 1 / 0 | 0.000048216 USD | 172 ms / 4.783 s | Jev selected direct confirmation; one delivered meal |
| Mateo, procurement tradeoff | 1 / 6 | 0.002603334 USD | 154 ms / 12.123 s | Gemini chose market-b and saved a valid short explanation |
| Elena, speed tradeoff | 1 / 6 | 0.002854914 USD | 174 ms / 12.490 s | Gemini chose market-a and saved a valid short explanation |

The exact router latencies and per-call measurements are retained in
`docs/evidence/adk-contract-verification.json`; the UI's provider-mix median is a
different measurement. Iris's real response selected both `direct` and `confirm`
with probability/confidence 1.0. Her run contains no offline or Vertex model
dispatches, no supplier lookup and no supplier selection question. The one-token
secondary-model fence remained in place. SQL enforced physical pantry sufficiency,
and the confirm/cook flow completed through twelve queue events.

Both Gemini cases used `VALIDATED` declared functions and produced legal finish
summaries without needing a correction. Offline ADK regression tests separately
replayed the actual invented-name and 574-character failures and verified bounded
correction, unchanged staged effects, exhausted correction denial and role/lease
isolation. Every live case denied raw stock, model-ledger and router-ledger reads
through its active restaurant login and passed stock, queue and replay checks.

Two earlier Jev-only probes stopped at confidence 0.82 and 0.72, with no secondary
model dispatch. They exposed a broad self-assessment question and unrelated
supplier context. The final revision classifies the requested kind of work and
retrieves supplier context only when relevant. It keeps the 0.85 confidence and
0.20 margin gates. Each follow-up required review, a new configuration/run and a
permanent marker; prior raw receipts and conservative reservations carry forward.
No failed request was resent or overwritten.

Across all three attempts, known token cost was **0.005610540 USD** and conservative
accounting was **0.06073198 USD**, below the shared **0.15 USD** cap. Final-attempt
usage alone was 0.005506464 USD. These are frozen-tariff calculations, with invoice
reconciliation pending. Billing was disabled afterward through the guarded
Terraform plan; the project and fifteen free foundation resources remain, with
no Cloud Run service or billable runtime in state. The local evidence preview has
no Jev key, ADC mount or paid Vertex gate.

This is a three-order repair smoke check. It establishes a real direct Jev
decision for this stocked-pantry case; it does not establish held-out quality,
production calibration, broad savings or automatic recovery of uncertain calls.

Official deployment references: [Gemini model lifecycle](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/model-versions),
[3.5 Flash-Lite capabilities](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/gemini/3-5-flash-lite),
[Vertex pricing](https://cloud.google.com/model-garden/pricing),
[Jev models and pricing](https://docs.typesafe.ai/models), and
[Jev typed questions](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives).

References: [ADK instructions and tools](https://adk.dev/agents/llm-agents/),

docs/AGENT-ANATOMY.md:
# Agent anatomy

Start with the team in one shared 3D delivery setting: stocked shelves, a packing
bench, loading dock, street and doorstep. Follow a store order from stock check
to picking, dispatch and delivery; recovery evidence then travels to the judge. Click any robot to inspect its parts. The whole
robot stays visible while the component highlights and its explanation appears.
Every hotspot stays available, so you can move directly between parts without
resetting your view. Anatomy is the complete agent reference: all 99 component
panels include **Full reference · read here**, which opens the corresponding
chapter beside the robot. Its section selector and related chapter links keep
reading inside the inspector; **Back to component reference** returns from a
related chapter. **Details & source** exposes the component's policy, evidence,
Agent Card where applicable, and source dialogs.

On a first visit, a skippable four-part tour explains the job, tools, guardrails
and recorded tests. Completion or dismissal is remembered in localStorage;
**Replay tour** starts it again. Reduced motion uses manual **Next** steps.
Selecting a part stops the tour, and **Back to team** returns to the order story.

**View options** contains **Reset view**, **Pause motion**, **Read guide** and
**Chapters**. Guide and chapter navigation remain optional: every selected
component still has its complete reference in the inspector.

The robot is an illustration of code, not a live actor or activity meter. Its
cab, tank, engine, arms and other parts map to the same manifest-backed panels.
The local Three.js renderer uses authored geometry, studio lighting and shadows;
there are no external models or network asset requests. **Pause motion** stops
the idle animation. Reduced motion disables idle movement and handoff animation. Hidden views
stop rendering, and leaving the chapter disposes the scene.

Keyboard users can Tab through component controls, use arrows between them,
and activate with Enter or Space. On the focused 3D canvas, arrows rotate and
plus/minus zoom within bounds that keep the body visible. A native component selector provides the same information.
If WebGL is unavailable or loses its context, the labelled SVG machine remains
fully usable. On a phone, the model stays above the selected component's details.
The desktop reading column keeps the same width for every component, so opening
or closing it never shifts the machine. It scrolls independently on desktop and
uses normal page flow on mobile. The physical part name leads each panel,
followed by its code topic and a plain-language explanation. Each component then leads with a real configuration or evidence number and short
plain-language bullets. Technical numbers, readable result tables and formatted
Agent Cards sit inside **Details & source**; memory retains its visual explorer. Selecting
a memory tab or reading a chapter preserves the chosen camera view.

Local Oxanium headings echo the machine's geometric form. The rest of the page
keeps IBM Plex text and numeric evidence; the shared UI typography is unchanged.
Font attribution and license are in web/fonts/README.md.

## What is technically hard

Keeping a believable agent inside a reliable system is the central problem.
Concurrent stock reservations must not oversell. A retried event must not deliver
or refund twice. A kitchen cannot cook an ingredient that has merely been promised.
A courier going offline mid-delivery must preserve physical custody. Memory must
help the current order without leaking another role's observations.

The design combines granular ADK tools, durable queue transactions, immutable run
definitions, scoped SQL identities, and A2A commands that carry work references.
The agents propose actions; tool implementations enforce the business facts.
SOUL text, retrieved context and incoming messages never grant permissions.

## Reading the machines

The cab explains the mission; the face explains persona; the arms expose tools.
The tank holds scoped memory. The cage explains guardrails, the gauge shows
budgets, and the engine shows deterministic versus model-backed decisions. The
antenna explains A2A and the separate read-only MCP server. Intake and exhaust
show event topics. The inspection sticker shows evidence; the wheels explain
where the code runs.

Each role has a stable purpose color on its body and top light, plus a distinct
symbol. The same color and symbol appear in the named role buttons and the
full-size inspector. Color is never the only identifier. A white ring marks the
current step's owner without changing that role's identity.

The team story is an **illustration, not live traffic**. A demo input creates
a dark-store order; the household robot models meal customers separately. A floor route connects physical handoffs; a raised dashed link shows the
controller-routed A2A request. Dotted review evidence leaves the delivered parcel
at the doorstep. **How agents communicate** explains the protocol legend. The judge reviews recovery decisions,
rather than approving every successful delivery. **Play order** runs one finite
journey; reduced motion offers **Next step** instead. On phones a single scene overview sits above six manual steps and nine named
role buttons. Meal-specific agents and customer service have their own stations
and remain inspectable alongside the main store flow. On the scene canvas,
arrows orbit and Home resets the viewpoint. Every role is also keyboard-accessible
through its named button; **Back to team** restores focus to that role.

The shared scene reuses a lower-detail version of the inspector's robot geometry.
It renders only when visible and changed, caps its render rate at 30 frames per
second and pixel ratio at 1.3, and disposes resources when leaving the chapter.
If 3D fails, a grouped floor plan retains all roles and manual story controls.
The inspector keeps its separate labelled SVG fallback.

The cab badge shows the role, and arm symbols represent up to four of that
role's actual tools. The gauge compares default USD model spending caps across
these templates: dark bars mean a zero default model budget, not an exhausted
balance. Customer service's default is $0.02 per run; optional ADK and cloud
profiles have their own limits. The inspector identifies the unit and scope.

## Inspecting memory

Select the storage tank to inspect the exact stored format, what reaches the
agent core, the local and optional Google Cloud paths, and their constraints.
The examples are explicitly synthetic. The page reads no private run memory,
database, deployment status or provider, and changing a preview changes no run.

**Record** shows PostgreSQL rows with a JSONB body, rather than a CSV, chat
transcript or file per agent. Select **Scope**, **Observation** or **History** to
see the corresponding fields. The body is selected initially; roles with several
observation kinds expose an **Observation type** selector. **Accepted body
schema** and **Complete example record** expose the full schema and record.
Examples are validated with the same role-specific Python contracts as the
runtime. Scope comes from the authenticated role and leased event; identity,
revision and provenance come from SQL. Times are simulation seconds.

**Core view** projects that same example through the real projection function:

| Profile | What reaches the core |
| --- | --- |
| `none` | An empty list; writes and audit history still exist. |
| `text` | A bounded string containing scope, facts and provenance. |
| `json` | A JSON object separating shared scope, fact bodies and provenance. |
| `typed` | Complete typed records with scope and provenance. |
| `semantic` | Typed records after ranking permitted candidates; the one-record preview demonstrates shape, not measured search quality. |

The recall diagram follows the leased event through the SQL scope gate, optional
ranking, SQL recheck and agent input. Restaurant ADK receives the selected
projection in its tool response. Deterministic workers use canonical facts for
decisions and audit; selecting a memory profile adds no model. The packaged
local embedding model makes no paid embedding API calls. SQL still rechecks
scope, lease, expiry and revision after ranking.

**Local / GCP** separates canonical records from their optional search index.
Locally, Docker Compose retains PostgreSQL data in `postgres-data`;
`agent_memory_facts` stores the observations, and `agent_semantic_vectors` holds
embedding arrays used by optional pgvector search. On Google Cloud, the
implemented Terraform path uses Cloud Run workers and Cloud SQL/PostgreSQL 17,
with optional Vertex Vector Search. The Vertex payload contains vectors, fact
IDs, scope/model hashes and expiry metadata, without raw fact text. Hashes are
filters, not encryption, and embeddings remain derived data.

The cloud view describes prerequisites rather than claiming a live deployment:
`active` and `enable_live` enable live storage, `live_ready` follows migration,
login and secret setup, and `enable_vector_search` adds Vertex. Authenticated
public API calls and scoped service-account grants govern access. Cloud SQL and
the one-replica Vertex deployment incur idle costs. The current lab disables SQL
backups and deletion protection; teardown can remove retained history. No
automatic Vertex TTL deletion or archival pipeline is implemented.

**Constraints** distinguishes recall budgets from storage capacity. An explicit
profile defaults to eight complete facts, 8,192 UTF-8 bytes and a 3,600-second
simulation lifetime; allowed bounds come from the profile schema. Per-role live
entry, body-byte and tool limits come from its manifest. An unset profile keeps
legacy recall behavior, not an implied explicit profile. Oversized facts are
omitted whole. Writes are idempotent for the same source event/type/subject;
conflicting content is rejected. Every recall uses a tool slot, and semantic
recall uses two fenced reads.

The lifecycle shows why expiry does not erase the audit trail or revive an older
revision. A disabled recall profile also preserves writes and audit history.
Scope prevents cross-order and cross-role recall; SQL functions and grants
enforce access, while the Python host and operator remain trusted. Observations
provide context, never new authority or proof that an observation is true.

Customer-service classification has a different, explicit view: a fresh ADK
session for each complaint, no persistent memory contract and no memory tools.
Durable request/result receipts prevent repeat billing; they are not recall.
Its separate Chaos turn receives only the affected order facts. A disclosure
explains the shared storage system without presenting it as a classifier feature.

Use Left/Right or Home/End within the four-tab list, or click a tab. The memory
chapter, source files and related references remain available in the same
inspector. The reference distinguishes local embedding/pgvector tests and mocked
Vertex request tests from a live GCP quality benchmark; no memory-specific
production pass rate, latency or monetary cost receipt is claimed.

## One authority, several profiles

Each repository-owned `role.json` is the capability ceiling. The published
[JSON Schema](../config/agents/role.schema.json) comes from the same Pydantic model
used to validate the files. A run snapshot can remove capabilities, never add
them. Restaurant tool profiles, main-service queue events and Chaos recovery
tools are declared in those same manifests. Fixed SQL and Python implementations
still enforce what each operation means; adding a string does not create a tool.

The restaurant has deterministic and ADK profiles, and the recovery judge has an
optional GCP profile. Customer-service classification is ADK with **no business
tools**; its separate Chaos turn has bounded recovery tools. Supply definitions
may choose a different SOUL or tighter budget and freeze it for that run. The
anatomy page describes checked-in templates, not private live run state.

## What the numbers prove

The [held-out release summary](evidence/heldout-release.json) records six offline
ADK arms, 72 cases and five attempts per case. pass^k counts cases where every
attempt passed. The all-pass bootstrap interval is degenerate; it is not a claim
of certainty on new tasks. Offline $0 cost and millisecond latency are not live
inference performance. Deterministic roles without a held-out ADK arm say so.

The [recorded Chaos shift](evidence/a2a-chaos-local.json) measures 1,148–1,765
**simulated seconds** to recover across five disruptions, with zero lost orders
in those cohorts. This includes delivery completion, not just replanning latency.
Cohorts overlap and do not establish a causal “orders saved” counterfactual.
Its €1.7215 per delivery is synthetic operating cost, not a model bill.

The [main consolidation receipt](evidence/main-consolidation.json) is historical
suite evidence. The current test result belongs to its own verification record;
this page never silently relabels old results as a fresh run.

## How the page stays honest

The [presentation builder](../src/delivery/anatomy_presentation.py) generates
plain labels, human number rows, evidence headlines and the narrated team flow.
The [data builder](../src/delivery/agent_anatomy.py) reads manifests and SOUL files,
uses the real Agent Card factory, inspects MCP declarations and loads dated eval
receipts. The [memory reference builder](../src/delivery/memory_reference.py)
validates synthetic bodies with the runtime contracts and generates all five
projections using the real memory profile function. It does not connect to a
database or provider. The browser renders the supplied facts and examples;
it does not maintain a second fact catalogue. A fingerprint covers
all source inputs, and contract tests compare panels, permissions, cards, event
edges, evidence and the published schema against their originating files.

The component readers include [agent implementation](AGENT-IMPLEMENTATION.md),
[ADK restaurants](ADK-RESTAURANT.md), [memory](AGENT-MEMORY.md),
[A2A](A2A.md), and [evaluations](AGENT-EVALS.md). Related chapter links inside a
component reader stay beside the robot; source links open inspectable dialogs.

# Agent evaluation workflow

Start the local stack (`make up`), then use Bash:

```bash
make eval-agents
```

The disposable checker runs the fixed battery **twice**, writes
`artifacts/health/latest-scenarios.json`, and exits nonzero for a failed or missing
case, changed source, or different repeated outcomes. `make health` includes this
command's evaluator alongside the complete test suite and static checks. Neither
command restarts the running app, Postgres or Redis. Open
[Health & evals → Agent evals](http://localhost:8010/health) to inspect the results.
Refreshing the page only reads receipts; it cannot execute a command.

All worlds use seed **731**, the committed synthetic catalogues/recipes and the
existing 32×32 city. They run in the dedicated **local `delivery_test` database**;
production database names, remote hosts and connection-string overrides are
rejected before creating a world. Model inference is disabled and ingredient
search uses its local adapter. There is no cloud endpoint option. The optional
GCP demo remains independent.

## Cases and scoring

The versioned contract is `data/evals/agent-scenarios.json`. Twelve scenarios
declare 49 criteria, each with a human-readable label and an exact typed expected
value. Booleans and integer counts are different measurements.

| Role | Scenario | Required behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Inventory | Two baskets, one unit | One reservation, one safe rejection; scoped stock visibility |
| Inventory | Delayed replenishment | Forecast units remain unavailable until actual receipt |
| Inventory | Crash before acknowledgement | Actual worker-process crash rolls back; lease retry has one effect |
| Restaurant | Available pantry | Deliver pizza without unnecessary sourcing |
| Restaurant | Market forwarding | Empty nearest market forwards flour request; ingredients arrive before cooking |
| Restaurant | Replacement declined | Record refusal and reject without cooking or consuming ingredients |
| Restaurant | Replacement approved | Household consent and kitchen approval both precede cooking |
| Dispatcher | Assignment race | Two workers contend for one courier; one job assigned, one deferred |
| Dispatcher | Traffic and retry | Congestion affects ETAs; retry needs approval; infeasible job is abandoned |
| Courier | Assignment authority | Other courier cannot read/accept brief or recall memory; motion waits for ACK |
| Courier | Dropout handoff | Replacement gets recorded parcel checkpoint, prior courier and source events |
| Courier | Physical arrival | Completion follows world arrival; route ETA equals edge duration sum |

A case passes only when **every declared criterion** passes and execution/cleanup
succeeds. A safe business rejection is a successful evaluation when rejection is
the specified outcome. Case and role scores are passed criteria divided by their
declared criteria; missing measurements receive no credit. The dashboard always
shows case failure counts alongside scores. Missing receipts have no score;
partial receipts cannot become a complete pass.

Scores are recomputed by the reader from the committed contract and measured
values. A receipt cannot supply its own expected values, headline pass count or
score. Unknown/duplicate cases, extra fields, malformed types, missing configuration
hashes, incorrect repeat hashes and mismatched manifest versions are rejected.

## What actually runs

`delivery.scenario_evals` creates eight small isolated fixture worlds. Agents are
the existing `LocalAgent` workers with their real per-run/store/role Postgres
logins, permissions, tool budgets, typed memory and durable queue leases. The
controller sets up stock, injects disruptions, advances virtual time and observes
results as a trusted operator. Agents communicate through queued events; the
evaluator does not replace their decisions with an oracle. Dispatcher contention
uses two concurrent workers, and inventory recovery kills a real subprocess.

The controller retires short-lived database identities and deletes its worlds in
`finally`, including after a fixture error. Failure receipts store fixed error
codes, never exception messages, SQL strings, connection URLs, event payloads or
memory bodies. The retained event trail contains only fixture-relative sequence,
topic, trace, queue state, attempts and scheduled simulation seconds. Fixture
sequence numbers are local to the receipt; deleted database events cannot be
opened later. Supply replay is checked before cleanup.

Two evaluations cannot interleave through the CLI: it holds a Postgres advisory
lock. Existing simulation runs in the application's `delivery` database are
unaffected. The test suite verifies that the battery leaves the pre-existing
test-run IDs and role identities unchanged, and that an injected fixture error
still cleans up without exposing its exception text.

## Reproducibility and limits

Receipts retain manifest version/hash, seed, effective configuration hashes, source
fingerprint, UTC creation time and a business-outcome hash for **each** repetition.
The hash includes typed observations and fixed error codes. It excludes wall time,
random run IDs, global SQL event IDs, and which racing worker wins: both possible
winners are valid, but one courier must still receive exactly one job.

Each repetition's observations are preserved and checked against its hash. A later
passing repeat cannot erase an earlier failed case. Each criterion keeps its first
explicit failure across repeats, otherwise its first missing measurement, otherwise
the final passing value. Criteria and event trails identify their repetition. An
omission cannot hide a measured failure from another repeat. Input hash drift also
produces a failed receipt, including when one setup attempt fails before creating
the world. A mismatch fails reproducibility even if both individual outcomes
otherwise meet the criteria. Starting the checker replaces any previous green
receipt with unmeasured evidence until the new battery finishes.

For a quicker diagnostic run after building the image:

```bash
docker compose run --rm --no-deps app python3 scripts/eval_agents.py --reproduce 1
```

The page labels a single run as repeatability **not measured**. Results from changed
sources or older than 24 hours remain historical. Rebuild the running app after
source changes so its fingerprint can match the checker. These are local receipts,
not signed attestations against a hostile host operator.

This is a fixed **development regression battery for rules-based agents**. It
measures coordinated business and permission behavior, not LLM reasoning quality,
production latency, cost per model decision, held-out generalization, or superiority
of one architecture/memory strategy. Those remain separate unmeasured benchmarks.

## Google-native model evaluation

[Committed-snapshot verification](evidence/google-native-evals.json) records the
test counts, scripted-arm metrics and limits of the latest local evaluation.

The native files are `evals/adk/restaurant.evalset.json` and
`evals/adk/customer_service.test.json`, with ten cases each. Install the pinned
runtime from `requirements.lock` (including `google-adk[eval]`), then run from the
repository root in Bash:

```bash
python3 -m pip install -r requirements.lock
python3 -m pip install --no-deps -e .
adk eval evals/adk/restaurant evals/adk/restaurant.evalset.json \
  --config_file_path evals/adk/test_config.json
adk eval evals/adk/customer_service evals/adk/customer_service.test.json \
  --config_file_path evals/adk/test_config.json
python3 -m pytest -q tests/test_adk_evalsets.py
python3 scripts/eval_agents.py --suite adk --repeat 3
```

`AgentEvaluator` and the CLI use the same EvalSet schema and deterministic
trajectory/response-match metrics. Both agents use `adk_offline.py`, with no
provider fallback. Tests deny provider initialization and HTTP; the CLI child also
denies sockets. Restaurant tools use in-memory fixtures and the production plan
schema. Actual SQL scope, admission, durability and migration-019 trace ingestion
remain covered by integration tests. Scripted classification is not evidence of
language understanding.

The repeated-arm receipt is `artifacts/evals/candidate.json`. `--repeat k`
(1–100) applies only to model arms, with a fresh session per attempt.
`--reproduce 1|2|3` independently controls SQL repeatability; `--suite all` runs
both. The default suite remains `scenarios` for compatibility with `make health`.
A container without Git can receive `DELIVERY_SOURCE_REVISION`; otherwise the
receipt is labelled unversioned. `make eval-adk` runs the model suite in Docker.

## Error analysis and categories

1. Start with the failing case, arm, repetition and category; reproduce locally.
2. Inspect the request's declared functions and the response's actual calls.
   Requests contain repeated history: count only new response calls.
3. Compare arguments and ordered steps against a reviewed reference. A correct
   final reply does not excuse an invented tool or a wrong supplier.
4. Check recovery evidence. A successful corrected tool response counts; an
   attempted retry without a response does not. Durable tool receipts capture
   terminal results when summarization is skipped.
5. Promote a minimal regression, rerun code checks, native evals and the original
   SQL integration test, then refine policy or prompts.

`delivery.trajectory_evals.read_trace(url, event_id)` reads one event from
`restaurant_model_calls` and `restaurant_tool_receipts` using an operator
connection. Migration 019 added request/response/latency columns; no new migration
or agent table grant is needed. `score_trajectory` reports multiset tool
precision/recall, exact-argument precision/recall, field differences, ordered LCS
match, extra/missing steps, model/tool step counts, incomplete dispatches and
recovery rate. No observed errors means recovery is null, not perfect.

The health taxonomy explicitly includes **schema**, **length** and
**invented_tool**. Schema checks reject malformed replies and unexpected
arguments. Length checks enforce the 1–500 character summary/reply boundaries.
Invented-tool checks use the declared capability set and never alias misspelled
names. These checks run before any semantic judge and spend no judge quota. Task
and trajectory correctness are separate gate categories.

## Promote stored evidence

Write an explicit reference containing tool names and arguments. Never treat a
failed output as its own desired answer. For example, using Bash:

```bash
mkdir -p artifacts/evals
cat > artifacts/evals/reference.json <<'JSON'
[{"name":"finish_decision","args":{"summary":"Compared the quotes."}}]
JSON
python3 scripts/promote_trace.py \
  --receipt artifacts/adk-route-comparison.json \
  --pointer /arms/3/evidence --event-id 123 \
  --reference artifacts/evals/reference.json \
  --id reviewed-cost-finish --description 'Reviewed terminal-tool regression' \
  --expect-category invented_tool
```

Replace 123 with the actual event and provide its complete reference. Alternatively
use `--stored-trace --event-id 123` with operator `DATABASE_URL` supplied through
the environment. Multi-event receipts require an event selector. Each promotion
creates the next `data/evals/golden/vN/` directory without overwriting prior
versions; the latest version of each case ID is evaluated. Review the diff before
committing. Reference arguments and descriptions still need privacy review. Raw
prompts, model thoughts and tool-result bodies are omitted; capability arguments
and minimal success/error classifications survive.

Golden case **001-cost-invented-finish** preserves a terminal-call excerpt from
the historical cost-mode receipt: `finish_finish_decision` instead of
`finish_decision`. Its expected result is an invented-tool rejection and zero
name recall. A passing negative regression means the scorer caught the known
failure, not that the historical run succeeded. The native `cost-source` case
separately verifies the current scripted agent's complete correct trajectory.

## Reliability, cost and latency

Every attempt is retained, including failures. **pass^k** is the empirical fraction
of distinct cases passing **all k** attempts. It is neither pass@k (at least one
success) nor the pooled pass rate raised to a power. Missing, duplicate or
unbalanced repetitions invalidate comparisons.

Seeded percentile bootstrap 95% intervals resample cases, keeping whole repeat
groups. Repeats are not extra independent cases. A one-case sample has no interval.
At all-pass/all-fail boundaries bootstrap intervals are degenerate; this does not
establish certainty about unseen tasks. Fixed development cases are not a random
production sample. Scripted pass^k/timings measure fixture stability, not live-model
reliability or production performance.

Cost per successful task divides the cost of all attempts, including failures,
by successful attempts. Unknown usage never becomes free; reservations provide a
separate conservative figure. Zero successes yield null. P95 latency includes
failures and uses an interpolated percentile. The recovery-judge script reports
these metrics too. Comparisons show main/candidate values and deltas; wall-clock
timing remains diagnostic because shared CI runners are noisy.

## PR gate and main baseline

The `evals` job runs on pull requests and main pushes without cloud credentials or
paid calls. Code checks precede native evals and three fresh scripted attempts per
case. Successful main runs store `eval-baseline-v1` for 90 days, including reviewed
`config/eval-gate.json` thresholds and source revision. PRs download the artifact
from the successful main run for their exact base SHA. PR changes cannot select
an alternate baseline or quietly weaken its stored thresholds.

CI collects model attempts with `--record-only`: quality mismatches stay in the
receipt for the statistical comparison instead of failing the collection step.
Runner exceptions, incomplete or duplicate repeats, inconsistent pass/category
values, and missing or failed golden regressions still fail immediately. The
ordinary CLI retains its nonzero exit for any failed attempt. Native ADK tests
copy applications into writable temporary directories, so the CLI can save its
`.adk` history even when container source files are read-only. Both CI jobs
explicitly disable telemetry and BigQuery export.

No baseline exists before the workflow first lands: that bootstrap run is explicitly
`baseline_missing`, with no quality comparison claim. Missing or expired artifacts
have the same status. Obtain a successful main run before relying on comparisons.

Comparisons require identical fixture hashes, modes, repeat counts, arms and case
IDs. Changed cohorts or corrupt receipts fail validation, not a statistical quality
test. Reference changes require a reviewed main baseline refresh. Saved headline
scores are ignored and recomputed from rows.

A quality regression requires all three:

- At least eight distinct paired cases.
- The lower end of the case-bootstrap 95% pass-rate-drop interval exceeds the
  permitted drop: zero for schema/length/invented tools, 0.05 for task/trajectory.
- An exact one-sided paired sign test passes family-wise 0.05, Bonferroni-adjusted
  across every arm and category.

A single fluctuation does not fail the statistical gate. Deterministic contract
failures and invalid artifacts still fail verification. Cost/latency deltas do not
fail the quality gate. One red/green PR comment is updated with evidence. A green
bootstrap or insufficient-evidence label is not proof of equivalence. Forks whose
tokens cannot comment retain Markdown as a job summary/artifact. The workflow
does not execute candidate code through `pull_request_target`.

```bash
python3 scripts/eval_gate.py --candidate artifacts/evals/candidate.json \
  --baseline artifacts/evals/main/candidate.json \
  --baseline-revision MAIN_COMMIT_SHA \
  --thresholds artifacts/evals/main/eval-gate.json
```

## Optional manual Vertex judge

`vertex-eval.yml` is `workflow_dispatch` only, main only, with an explicit `paid`
input. Configure the `vertex-evals` environment variables `GCP_EVAL_PROJECT`,
`GCP_EVAL_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_PROVIDER` and `GCP_EVAL_SERVICE_ACCOUNT` with an identity
authorized for Vertex evaluation. It judges existing synthetic customer replies
from `data/evals/customer-replies.json`, without generating candidates.

`cloud_ai.py` sends the documented `evaluateInstances` pointwise request with
`gemini-2.5-flash-lite`, one sample, no thinking, at most 256 output tokens, an
8 KiB request and a 30-second timeout. It bypasses the SDK's internally retrying
batch helper. No model fallback is allowed. A SQLite ledger reserves USD 0.01
before each request, enforcing USD 0.05 per run; even if twelve calls are
requested, money admits at most five. Reservations remain charged after errors
and timeouts. Service usage/invoice cost is unknown: this is an admission ceiling
with conservative overhead, not a billing guarantee. Workflow reruns are disabled;
a new explicitly authorized dispatch starts a new scope.

The transport and Google wire schema are tested with mocks. **No live Vertex
evaluation verified this change.** Check service availability, IAM and regional
support on the first manual run. Pricing checked 2026-10-29: Flash-Lite 2.5 text
input/output are USD 0.10/0.40 per million tokens, below Flash-Lite 3.1's
USD 0.25/1.50. Review the pinned model and reservation before changing tariffs.

## Later: simulated users

`evals/adk/personas/customer_service.scenarios.json` contains valid ADK
ConversationScenario scaffolds for order status, refunds over EUR 100 and prompt
injection using the EVALUATOR persona. They are schema-tested, but excluded from
evalsets, CI and the manual judge. No simulator model is enabled. Activation needs
its own budget and a multi-turn customer agent; today's advice interface is one turn.

## Google references checked 2026-10-29

The implementation was checked against pinned ADK 2.13.0 and these official docs:

- [ADK evaluation](https://google.github.io/adk-docs/evaluate/)
- [ADK criteria](https://google.github.io/adk-docs/evaluate/criteria/)
- [ADK user simulation](https://google.github.io/adk-docs/evaluate/user-sim/)

- [Google Cloud model pricing](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/pricing)

# Shared local inventory agent foundation

This is the original inventory-slice reference, with later memory clarifications.
For the complete source-reviewed eight-role implementation and optional cloud
judge, read [Agent implementation](AGENT-IMPLEMENTATION.md) and
[GCP component inventory](GCP-COMPONENTS.md). The original 10×10 city and test counts
below describe that historical checkpoint, not today's complete 32×32 demo.

The shared factory also powers courier and judge roles in the
[expanded fleet recovery scenario](FLEET-RECOVERY.md), with scoped exported briefings
kept separate from private memory.

Implemented and verified 2026-10-23. The same factory now also supports isolated
fulfillment and dispatcher roles: see [basket-to-delivery flow](DELIVERY-FLOW.md).
The original inventory scenario creates five inventory agents,
one per fictional store. Everything runs locally; model calls, tokens and dollars
are capped at zero. The existing last-unit, delayed-replenishment and real worker
crash scenario now uses this foundation.

## Reusable building block

- `config/agents/inventory/role.json`: strict role, subscriptions, emitted topics,
  fixed tool names and numeric limits. `SOUL.md` holds versioned behavioral guidance.
- `src/delivery/agent_specs.py`: immutable validated contract and definition hash.
- `src/delivery/agent_access.py`: trusted operator provisions independent temporary
  database logins, binds each to one run/store, and freezes the definition.
- `src/delivery/agent_runtime.py`: authenticated factory, bounded tool registry,
  inventory policy, private memory and decision evidence.
- `src/delivery/queue.py`: leases, priorities, retries, dead letters, idempotency,
  lineage and backpressure. State effects, outgoing messages and ACK commit together.

Edit the inventory role/soul for a **new** run; existing runs retain their frozen
database snapshot. Compose mounts the definitions read-only. To use a separate
definition directory in the host environment:

```sh
delivery lab-demo --role-dir config/agents/inventory
```

The current deterministic policy consumes scoped facts and memory. Soul text is
recorded guidance, not an LLM interpreter. Copying the definition specializes this
supported inventory role; adding dispatcher/director authority requires a reviewed
server policy and database permissions, not just a new prompt.

## Permissions and information boundaries

Each run/store receives a distinct non-superuser login without role creation or
row-security bypass. Forced PostgreSQL row security derives scope from authenticated
`session_user`, rather than payloads or writable session settings. Agents cannot
read other stores/runs, the operator's world snapshot, bindings or full catalogue.
Catalogue access projects only their stocked products and removes source URLs.

Tools implicitly bind the authenticated scope. Parameters cannot override run,
store, owner or memory namespace. The registry exposes inventory operations,
memory reads/writes and queue publication. It exposes no raw SQL, filesystem,
network, arbitrary code execution or direct-agent call tool. Accepted and emitted
topics have server-owned allowlists. Other roles' cooperation must use events.

The crash subprocess receives its scoped database URL and essential OS environment
only; operator/test database URLs and cloud credentials are excluded. Credentials
are not included in exported evidence. Logins are retired when the run finishes or
fails normally; budget and identity evidence remains inspectable.

The operator API/UI intentionally inspects all stores. Operator code, the host and
fixed Python policy implementation are trusted. This is a database/tool boundary
for those policies, not an OS sandbox for arbitrary Python supplied by an agent.
M1 still uses its original shared database account.

## Memory and budgets

Private typed facts carry role, order, source event, revision, observed simulation
time and expiry. Recall derives scope from the current incoming lease and excludes
other orders, roles, expired facts and superseded revisions. Agents cannot browse
the underlying history or decision bodies. Writes enforce per-entry size, entry
count and aggregate bytes, including concurrent writes. Default caps are 32 live
entries and 16,384 bytes; default TTL is one simulated hour. Canonical stock remains
authoritative when memory is stale or poisoned. Vector retrieval and shared summaries
are future work.

See [memory implementation and enterprise references](AGENT-MEMORY.md) for the
typed schemas, selective recall, audited history and proposed evaluation sequence.

Original inventory per-agent caps: 100 event attempts, eight reserved tool slots per attempt,
400 slots per run. Aggregate caps are 500 attempts and 2,000 slots per run. The
database durably reserves an attempt and its full slot allowance before handling.
Crashes do not refund reservations; repeated reservation of the same attempt is
idempotent. Explicit dead-letter replay advances the attempt and gets a new ticket.
Actual committed tool calls are recorded separately from reserved capacity.

Tools require a live fenced lease and budget ticket. Waiting for locks cannot
extend authority beyond lease expiry. Budget denial produces no inventory effects.
The inventory profile requires zero model budgets. The optional `judge-gcp` profile
is a separate supported exception with durable call/token admission; its
`model_usd: 0` field must not be presented as a monetary spending ceiling.

## City and inspection

The versioned city has 100 connected nodes in a 10×10 grid and 360 directed adjacent
edges, spaced 500 metres apart. Five stores, depot, supplier, fuel and charging
anchors occupy the grid. Traffic and vehicle movement remain later work.

At `/lab`, choose a store to inspect its scope, role hash, frozen soul/tools,
reserved and committed work, and private-memory usage. Decisions expand to show
scoped observations and tool records. Saved older city evidence stays renderable.
Private Bakiano sample rows remain ignored and are not included in Git or images.

## Verified evidence and remaining work

At the original inventory checkpoint, the Linux Compose suite passed **67 tests**,
Ruff and mypy. Real non-superuser
connections test cross-store/run reads and writes, forged scope, forbidden tables,
role switching, budget modification, private memory, concurrent budget reservation,
TTL/capacity, poisoned memory, definition freezing and replay charging. Worker tests
exercise actual exits before and after commit, lease fencing and stock conservation.

The dated local Bakiano CLI scenario recovered exit 73 on attempt two and passed
stock and budget invariants. Chrome checks passed for map edges, store-specific
agent inspection, crash/race/delay checkpoints and desktop/mobile layout.

Still deferred: durable controller restart/resumption and abrupt-death cleanup,
independently supervised continuous workers, configurable hierarchies, pgvector,
ADK and held-out architecture/model comparisons. Additional delivery/supply roles,
typed memory, supply business-state replay and an optional GCP judge are now
implemented slices. Current [role eval evidence](AGENT-EVALS.md) records 392 passing
tests and twelve reproducible local scenarios; broader production readiness is
not established by those results.
