# How this project's agents are built

Source review: 2026-10-28. This describes the executable implementation, not an
illustrative ADK design. Start with this document, then read the
[GCP component inventory](GCP-COMPONENTS.md) and
[enterprise architecture decisions](ENTERPRISE-GCP.md).

## The agent object

An agent is a frozen `LocalAgent` containing an authenticated `AgentScope`, a
validated `RoleSpec`, its scoped database identity and, for an explicitly enabled
GCP judge, a gateway origin. Its public work loop is `claim()` → `process(event)`.
The shared class is in [agent_runtime.py](../src/delivery/agent_runtime.py).
`create_inventory_agent` is an alias of `create_agent`, not a separate framework.

Most agents use fixed Python decision policies. Restaurants can instead select
the [Google ADK adapter](ADK-RESTAURANT.md), with editable prompts/SOUL and granular
tools. Its current model is a scripted offline fixture; Gemini is not enabled.
Inventory arithmetic, sourcing,
consent, route selection and custody are enforced by domain code and SQL. The
recovery judge is the previously live-verified Google model path; restaurants now
also have a disabled-by-default, budgeted native Vertex adapter. The city is a realistic test
environment for those boundaries; running a city is not itself an LLM workload.

| Building block | Actual implementation | What it guarantees |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Definition | Canonical `role.json` manifests, [JSON Schema](../config/agents/role.schema.json), `RoleSpec` and `RoleLimits` in [agent_specs.py](../src/delivery/agent_specs.py) | Strict fields, frozen objects, bounded limits and manifest-owned tool/topic subsets |
| Provisioning | `inventory_access`, `role_access`, `supply_access` in [agent_access.py](../src/delivery/agent_access.py) | Trusted controller creates a login, binds its scope and snapshots definition/hash |
| Factory | `create_agent` in [agent_runtime.py](../src/delivery/agent_runtime.py) | Reads scope from authenticated SQL functions and checks the saved definition hash |
| Work delivery | `Queue` and [queue capability migration](../sql/migrations/014_queue_capability.sql) | Addressed claims, lease fencing, priorities, due time, retry/backoff and dead letters |
| Action boundary | `ScopedTools.invoke` and role-specific SQL functions | Fixed callable registry; authenticated scope and live budget/lease checks |
| Memory | [typed_memory.py](../src/delivery/typed_memory.py), [typed-memory migration](../sql/migrations/015_typed_memory.sql) | Typed observations, current-context recall, source events, expiry and revision history |
| Accountability | Decisions, tool receipts, memory read/write receipts and queued lineage | Inspect what the worker observed and changed, with business replay where implemented |

## From editable definition to an authenticated worker

1. The operator edits a supported role's `role.json` and `SOUL.md`, or a supply
   blueprint's agent/entity definitions. The canonical `role.json` is the only
   permission ceiling; blueprint and runtime profiles can narrow its grants.
   Editing a manifest cannot create a new tool implementation. SOUL text never
   grants permissions.
2. The loader validates the definition and resolves SOUL text. `RoleSpec.digest`
   hashes its canonical resolved JSON, including that text. Role-file SOUL paths
   are constrained to the supported definition directory.
3. The trusted controller creates a restricted PostgreSQL login per run/namespace.
   `agent_bindings` stores the login, run, namespace, agent ID, definition and hash;
   budget tables store the corresponding limits. Passwords stay in the controller's
   process and scoped connection objects, not in prompts or exported evidence.
4. `create_agent(dsn, agent_mode=..., cloud_endpoint=...)` calls `agent_scope()` and
   `agent_definition()` as that login. It rejects missing bindings, invalid hashes,
   incompatible judge modes and a cloud judge without an endpoint.
5. Later blueprint/role-file edits affect new runs. The running agent reads its
   frozen database definition. New supply runs additionally snapshot recipes,
   demand schedules and entity settings; blueprint updates use revision checking.
6. Normal run completion/failure retires the temporary logins through
   `retire_inventory_access`. Definitions and evidence can remain for inspection.
   Abrupt controller death still needs a durable supervisor/reaper.

For supply agents, [supply_models.py](../src/delivery/supply_models.py) defines
`AgentDefinition` and `EntityDefinition`; `supply_access` converts the frozen
run/entity settings into `RoleSpec`. They do not load restaurant/market role files
from `config/agents`. Display name, SOUL, simulated latency, search options and
bounded limits are editable. A fictional display name does not change a principal.

## What SOUL means today

SOUL is versioned and inspectable guidance. **The deterministic policies do not
interpret it.** Editing it does not teach a courier a new strategy or change stock
arithmetic. Business settings such as stock, hours, consent and latency have
explicit implemented effects.

The GCP judge does not receive its local role SOUL either. Its cloud container
has a separate fixed `systemInstruction` and `PROMPT_VERSION` in
[gateway.py](../infra/gcp-ai/gateway.py). Consequently, a local SOUL hash is not
proof of the exact model prompt. Cloud experiments must retain the gateway prompt
version/image digest as well as the local role definition hash.

The restaurant ADK adapter assembles platform instructions, the frozen role prompt
and SOUL, then supplies scoped tools and current-order recall. Its two offline
profiles demonstrate that instructions reach the actual ADK function-calling loop.
The scripted model implements those fixture strategies; this is not evidence of
generative-model quality. Permissions and budgets remain enforced independently.
Other roles and the cloud judge keep the behavior described above.

## Roles, namespaces and tools

`store` in internal binding tables is a namespace field; it is not always a shop.
Every role has typed `memory.read` and `memory.write`. The domain tools below are
prefixed exactly as their runtime registry names indicate.

| Role | Binding namespace | Domain tools | Typed fact kind |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Inventory | `store-N` | `inventory.read/reserve/release/delay/receive` | `inventory.reservation`, `inventory.shipment` |
| Fulfillment | `fulfillment:store-N` | `fulfillment.read/pick` | `fulfillment.progress` |
| Dispatcher | `dispatcher:fleet` | `dispatch.read/assign/complete/recover/defer` | `delivery.progress` |
| Courier | `courier:<fleet-id>` | `courier.read/accept` | `courier.commitment` |
| Judge | `judge:fleet` | `judge.read/review` | `recovery.verdict` |
| Household | Entity ID | `supply.read/command` | `household.order` |
| Restaurant | Entity ID | `supply.read/command` | `restaurant.order` |
| Market | Entity ID | `supply.read/command` | `market.request` |

That table describes the default deterministic supply workers. An ADK restaurant
uses `restaurant.*` capabilities listed in the [ADK chapter](ADK-RESTAURANT.md)
and a separate restricted PostgreSQL group. It cannot call `supply.command` or
read the legacy broad supply context. Its typed memory contract remains unchanged.

Workflow roles use `queue.publish` within their topic/recipient policy. Supply
commands produce a fixed SQL outbox; the agent cannot choose arbitrary recipients.
Although `supply.search` is declared in the supply authority contract, it is not a
`ScopedTools.invoke` implementation. Restaurant/market search is the separate
authenticated `search_for_agent` path in
[supply_search_service.py](../src/delivery/supply_search_service.py); the fixed
`SupplyPolicy` does not automatically call it. Optional Jev search and its budgets
are separate from the GCP judge.

Examples of the actual queue contracts are inventory `basket.requested` →
`basket.reserved`, fulfillment → `basket.ready`, dispatcher → `courier.briefed`,
courier → `courier.accepted`, and failed delivery → judge `recovery.reviewed`.
Complete accepted/emitted sets live in each canonical `role.json`; the Madrid
service's queue topics are recorded in its `service_events` profile.
No role exposes a direct agent-call tool. Simulated phone calls are typed queued
messages, not telephony sessions or free-form LLM conversations.

## The existing HTTP communication endpoints

These local supply routes are implemented in
[supply_api.py](../src/delivery/supply_api.py). Their common prefix is
`/api/supply/runs/{run}/agents/{agent_id}`:

| Method / suffix | Authentication and behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /channel` | Operator `X-Operator-Key`, matching configured `DELIVERY_OPERATOR_KEY`; issues a one-hour bearer channel for an active agent |
| `POST /claim` | Scoped bearer channel; claims an addressed queued event and returns its event/lease/attempt envelope |
| `POST /messages` | Scoped bearer plus matching envelope; processes the existing leased event, never arbitrary caller-supplied message content |
| `POST /calls` | Same mechanism, restricted to an owned household-intent lease |
| `POST /search` | Scoped bearer/envelope plus bounded query and frozen provider choice; restaurant/market search path |
| `POST /memory/recall` | Scoped bearer/envelope; consumes a tool allowance; only supported type/limit filters |
| `GET /memory` | Authenticated legacy route returns 410; broad memory retrieval is unavailable |

Envelope fields are `event_id`, `lease_token` and `attempt`. Database checks still
fence stale leases even after HTTP authentication. Blueprint, run/order history,
agent inspection and replay endpoints are separate **trusted operator views**;
they are not tools available to an agent.

Channel-token hashes, active agents and claimed HTTP lease references are currently
process-local dictionaries. They do not survive a restart or provide a shared
identity layer for several API replicas. Base Compose binds the app to loopback;
the Host/origin checks are local-demo safeguards, not enterprise authentication.
A cloud deployment needs workload OIDC/IAM and durable lease/controller handling;
publishing the existing operator API unchanged would expose broader inspection.

## One event, including the transaction boundaries

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Trusted controller
    participant A as Scoped LocalAgent
    participant Q as PostgreSQL queue
    participant T as Domain tools and memory
    C->>Q: Publish an addressed event
    A->>Q: Claim with role subscriptions
    Q-->>A: Event, attempt and fenced lease token
    A->>Q: Reserve attempt and full tool allowance
    Note over A,Q: Reservation commits before handling
    A->>Q: Begin effects transaction and validate lease
    A->>T: Read authoritative facts and current-context memory
    A->>T: Execute allowed actions and append memory revisions
    A->>Q: Record decision and publish outgoing events
    A->>Q: ACK in the same transaction
    Note over Q,T: Commit together, or roll back together
```

`LocalAgent.process` first commits the attempt/tool reservation. Optional GCP mode
then prepares a durable scoped request, commits its single-dispatch admission,
closes the worker's database connection, invokes the provider and saves its result
in a separate short transaction. Then `Queue.process` obtains the run
advisory lock and event row lock, checks the fence, reloads the authoritative
payload and invokes `handle`. The handler selects `InventoryPolicy`, `SupplyPolicy`
or `WorkflowPolicy`/`FleetPolicy` and records the decision before ACK commits.

Handler failure or lease expiry rolls back domain changes, memory, decision,
outgoing events and transactional tool charges. Failure scheduling happens
separately. Durable attempt/model reservations are not refunded. Deduplication
and domain invariants provide idempotent business effects; they do not establish
exactly-once external inference or billing. See [queue.py](../src/delivery/queue.py).

**Durable cloud path:** `FleetPolicy.cloud_judgement` only consumes a saved result;
it cannot invoke the provider. The effects transaction compares the saved context,
proposal, memory and simulated time with current authoritative observations before
SQL independently checks feasibility. A retry of the same source event reuses a
saved result without another model charge. An abandoned in-flight invocation has
an unknown outcome and fails closed rather than automatically resending. The
request snapshot and its preparatory read/tool receipts commit independently of
the final effects transaction. See [durable inference](DURABLE-INFERENCE.md),
[orchestration](../src/delivery/durable_inference.py) and the
[request state machine](../sql/migrations/016_durable_inference.sql).

## Permissions and memory are enforced outside the prompt

Logins are non-superuser, cannot create databases/roles, replicate or bypass RLS.
Scope derives from PostgreSQL `session_user`, not a model-supplied store ID or
mutable connection setting. Inventory can inspect its own run/store stock through
RLS. Other domain roles receive narrow functions/projections rather than raw stock
tables. Tools require a live lease, supported event and durable budget ticket.

Typed memory writes derive owner, order/shipment, subject, source event, revision
and observation time on the server. Bodies are limited to 2 KiB; TTL is 1–86,400
simulated seconds, additionally constrained by the role's live entry/byte caps.
Recall defaults to eight facts, permits at most sixteen and bounds complete result
envelopes to 8 KiB. Market recall is ingredient-request-specific; courier recall
also matches the assignment attempt. A newer expired revision suppresses older
values. Raw current/history/legacy memory tables are denied to agents.

Expiry controls recall eligibility; it does **not** erase audit history. Revisions
and decision inspection remain until trusted cleanup. There is no pgvector search,
cross-order learning, automatic summary consolidation or managed Memory Bank.
[Memory contracts and retention](AGENT-MEMORY.md) contain the detailed semantics.

The controller, operator UI/API, host and fixed Python policies are trusted. One
Python process can hold several scoped connections; this is not a container/OS
sandbox for hostile Python. M1 also retains its older shared-account runtime.
Enterprise workload identities and process boundaries must complement these
database controls; adding an ADK subagent object alone provides neither.

## Budgets and reproducible evidence

The original inventory profile has 100 attempt reservations, eight tool slots per
attempt, 400 per run, 32 live facts and 16,384 live body bytes. These are not global
defaults for every business role. Supply sessions set aggregate allowances of
12,000 attempts/48,000 tool slots and resolve larger dispatcher/courier profiles
before freezing them. Inspect the saved definition and budget for a particular run.

The optional [judge-gcp definition](../config/agents/judge-gcp/role.json) permits six
model calls and 50,688 reserved tokens. Each request reserves 8,448 tokens
(8,192 input + 256 output). `model_usd: 0` is a schema literal, **not a working
dollar ceiling** for paid GCP mode. Gateway-wide monetary admission remains a gap.

```bash
make health
make eval-agents
```

The [role battery](AGENT-EVALS.md) runs actual scoped agents on twelve fixed
scenarios and scores 49 declared criteria. The 2026-10-28 receipt records 392
passing tests and matching repeated seed-731 outcomes. This is development
regression/isolation evidence, not proof of LLM quality, scalability or production
readiness. [GCP live verification](GCP-VERIFICATION.md) is a separate dated record.

# Agent memory: records, recall and storage

The durable memory boundary is implemented in Python/Postgres. The optional
[restaurant ADK adapter](ADK-RESTAURANT.md) uses this typed recall through a scoped
function tool; its ADK session is fresh per event and contains no other order's
conversation. Its default model is an offline fixture; explicit paid experiments
use native Gemini on Vertex and optional Jev routing. We do not run LangGraph,
OpenAI Agents SDK or a managed Memory Bank. The references below guide the design;
we have not benchmarked this project as state of the art.
The default city remains local, with model providers disabled.

## What exists today

| Layer | Current implementation | Boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Operational truth | Transactional stock, reservations, orders and delivery custody in Postgres | A memory entry cannot change stock or override feasibility checks |
| Agent recall | Typed, versioned observations for the authenticated role and current incoming order | Lease-bound database functions; latest unexpired matching facts only |
| Audit | Queue lineage, decisions and replay facts; successful memory writes commit with the decision and ACK | Operator inspection is broader than agent recall; it is not an agent tool |
| Memory changes | Append-only revisions retain owner, order, source event, observation time, expiry and previous revision | Operator reconstructs diffs; write receipts never expose previous bodies |
| Conversation | Named fictional participants and readable queue messages, with memory changes at the receiving step | Presentation only; no invented LLM dialogue or changes to security principals |

The old `last:<order>` JSON entries remain operator history; agents cannot read or
write that legacy table. They are not automatically promoted to typed facts.
Order history can inspect archived writes after live recall expires.
Older records without a captured baseline show **previous value unavailable**;
expiry is distinguished from an active previous value. Scheduled delivery time
is labeled **Due** when the actual enqueue simulation time cannot be established.

## Typed memory and selective recall

Nine version-one contracts cover inventory reservations and shipment observations,
fulfillment progress, dispatcher progress, courier commitments, recovery verdicts,
household orders, restaurant orders and supermarket requests. Bodies reject
unknown fields and invalid values in both Python and Postgres. The SQL catalogue
retains each schema; a regression test checks that Python and SQL agree.

`memory.write(kind=..., body=..., ttl_seconds=3600)` records an observation of a
scoped tool outcome. The server supplies the owner, run, context, subject, source
event, observation time, revision and expiry. Callers cannot supply these fields.
Repeated writes for the same source/type/subject are idempotent; different content
or TTL under that source is rejected. Per-agent live count/body-byte caps are
serialized across concurrent writes. History persists until trusted operator
cleanup of the run/source events; expiry removes eligibility for recall, not audit.
The local supplier policy keeps pending reservations for one simulated hour and
finished/forwarded requests for one minute. Those short-lived terminal revisions
still suppress the older reservation and remain in history. This prevents closed
ingredient requests from occupying the default live-memory budget for an hour;
the capacity limit itself is unchanged.

`memory.read(kinds=None, limit=8)` has no order or namespace parameter. SQL derives
them from the authenticated session and current leased event. Supermarkets recall
only the current ingredient request; couriers only the addressed assignment
attempt. Results include source events, observation/expiry times and revision IDs,
with a maximum of 16 facts and 8 KiB for the full result envelopes. These canonical reads use exact indexed filters. An explicit semantic profile
adds ranking after this authorization step and rechecks SQL before returning facts. A newer expired revision suppresses
older revisions even if their original TTL has not elapsed. Repeatable-read and
serializable transactions are rejected so old snapshots cannot revive history.

Agent HTTP callers use `POST .../agents/{agent}/memory/recall` with their bearer
token and current event ID, lease token and attempt. Only type/limit filters are
accepted. The previous broad `GET .../memory` returns 410. HTTP recall consumes a
reserved tool slot, as does a direct SQL call. Decisions record which fact IDs and
versions were recalled; the operator can inspect this in an order's memory section.

Agents have no table access to current or historical memories or decision bodies.
Queue claim/ACK/failure/publication and tool charges use fixed database functions;
raw lease extension, event forgery, budget-counter resets and history browsing are
denied. These restrictions also cover existing role logins after migration.

Facts remain observations: stock, consent, routing and custody are authoritative in
the domain database. The fixed worker commits memory, decision, outbox and ACK in
one transaction. This atomic worker behavior is tested; SQL source authenticity
does not certify that an arbitrary authorized client's observation is true or
force a client to combine separate SQL statements into one transaction. The host,
operator API and fixed Python code remain trusted; agents have no arbitrary SQL,
network or code tool. This is not an OS sandbox for hostile code.

## Selectable per-agent memory

Each shared role template or individual entity can select a memory profile in
`/restaurant-lab`. Entity overrides are frozen at run creation. Leaving the profile
unset preserves legacy recall. A profile changes the context an agent receives,
with these bounded choices:

| Mode | Context returned to an ADK restaurant or Jev router | Useful when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `none` | No prior facts | The current event and authoritative tools are sufficient |
| `text` | Concise factual lines with source, version and expiry references | A few observations fit naturally in a short prompt |
| `json` | Compact structured facts with a scope envelope and provenance | A small machine-readable record is sufficient |
| `typed` | Canonical typed fact envelopes | Decisions need explicit revisions, relationships and expiry |
| `semantic` | Authorized facts ranked by meaning, returned as typed envelopes | Relevant prior observations need ranking within the same order |

All modes keep canonical typed writes and revision history for audit. `none`
disables recall, not evidence retention. Text and JSON are projections of scoped
facts, not an unrestricted scratchpad or a second source of truth. The model
cannot pick a foreign namespace, write arbitrary JSON, fetch the whole chat or
turn a memory statement into inventory authority. Selecting a mode does not provision infrastructure. Semantic mode needs the
packaged local embedding model and pgvector, or explicitly configured Vertex
Vector Search. No summarizer or managed Memory Bank is used.

Profiles cap the number of facts (1–8), complete UTF-8 representation bytes
(256–8,192), and maximum fact lifetime (60–86,400 simulated seconds). Defaults are
eight facts, 8 KiB and one hour. SQL applies role/order/request/attempt scope,
expiry and the lower profile bounds before Python formats the result. Whole facts
are omitted when they cannot fit; values and source references are never truncated
or summarized. The lifetime setting caps a writer's requested TTL and cannot
extend an existing shorter retention policy. Canonical facts remain available to
the trusted stale-result fence even if the model sees a text or JSON projection.

SQL wrappers retain the original public function identities and call private typed
implementations. Agent identities cannot execute those private helpers to bypass
the selected profile. Validation covers Python definitions and frozen database
bindings. Historical agents without a profile keep their previous behavior.

Sources: [memory profile and projections](../src/delivery/memory_profiles.py),
[database profile enforcement](../sql/migrations/024_agent_memory_modes.sql),
[profile and isolation checks](../tests/test_memory_profiles.py).

## What a memory is

A memory is a row in PostgreSQL's `agent_memory_facts`, with typed identity and
scope columns and a `body` stored as JSONB. It is not a CSV, a separate file per
agent or an unrestricted chat transcript. `agent_memory_types` holds the accepted
body schemas. The `agent_memory_current` view selects the latest revision.
The Anatomy storage tank renders a synthetic example for the selected role,
validates its body with the real schema, and formats each view with the actual
`project_memory` function. It never reads private run memory.

Scope (run, store/entity, role, context and subject) and history (row ID, version,
source event, observation time, expiry and previous revision) are server assigned.
`fact_id` in recall corresponds to the SQL row's `id`. Simulation seconds govern
expiry. One JSONB body can occupy at most 2,048 SQL-serialized bytes; this is
distinct from the whole recall envelope's 8 KiB limit. Role manifests separately
cap live entries and body bytes across the entity.

## Semantic recall and the core

The worker first gets canonical candidates through its fenced SQL recall.
Semantic mode embeds the query and those candidates locally using
`BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5` (384 dimensions), then ranks only that authorized set.
Queries are bounded to 512 UTF-8 bytes and the candidate set to eight facts.
The SQL gate runs again after ranking: invented, foreign, stale or expired IDs
cannot become agent input. This costs two fenced memory reads, so both tool
slots must be available. Missing dependencies and invalid embeddings fail closed.

An ADK restaurant receives the selected projection through its scoped tool
response. Deterministic policies retain canonical facts for decision provenance;
selecting a profile does not turn them into model-driven agents. The customer
service classifier has fresh complaint sessions, no persistent recall contract,
and durable inference receipts for billing/idempotency. Its chaos turns see only
affected-order facts. Repeated customer complaints across different orders are
**not** supported by this memory scope.

The three checked-in recall cases exercise repeated reservation, stock refusal
and expiry within one order, against a no-memory baseline. Tests cover real local
embeddings/pgvector and isolation. Vertex HTTP payloads and filters use a mock;
there is no live Vertex quality benchmark or published memory-specific pass-rate,
latency or cost receipt. Audit includes backend, model, query hash and returned
fact IDs. Zero paid embedding API calls does not imply free infrastructure.

## Local and Google Cloud storage

Locally, Compose's `postgres-data` volume retains canonical facts. The optional
`agent_semantic_vectors` cache stores JSONB numeric arrays keyed by fact ID and
model; SQL casts them to pgvector for exact cosine ranking. It is not a global
unfiltered nearest-neighbor index.

The optional GCP live path keeps canonical facts in Cloud SQL PostgreSQL 17.
Cloud Run uses scoped database logins and role service accounts. Terraform requires
`active` and `enable_live` for storage, plus `live_ready` after migrations, logins
and secret versions before starting services.

With `enable_vector_search`, Vertex stores 384-number vectors, model-prefixed
fact IDs, opaque scope/model hashes and expiry metadata. No raw fact body or
query text is sent to Vertex; the query vector is sent. Embeddings are derived
data, and hashes are filters rather than encryption. The public-network endpoint
requires authenticated API calls through Application Default Credentials.
Terraform grants the configured api, restaurant and dispatcher identities
bounded index-update/query permissions.

Cloud SQL and the single-replica Vertex deployment have idle costs. The public
replay needs neither. `active=false` removes these resources; documentation never
starts them or claims a deployment is running. The lab Terraform currently
disables SQL backups and deletion protection. TTL removes recall eligibility,
not history or Vertex datapoints. There is no automatic Vertex TTL deletion or
archival pipeline. Teardown can remove retained audit data.

Implementation: [typed contracts](../src/delivery/typed_memory.py),
[generated public reference](../src/delivery/memory_reference.py),
[scoped runtime](../src/delivery/agent_runtime.py),
[ADK tool projection](../src/delivery/adk_restaurant.py),
[typed SQL](../sql/migrations/015_typed_memory.sql),
[semantic interface](../src/delivery/semantic_memory.py),
[semantic SQL](../sql/migrations/031_semantic_memory.sql),
[Cloud SQL and live workers](../infra/production/live.tf),
[Vertex infrastructure](../infra/production/vector.tf),
[semantic tests](../tests/test_semantic_memory.py),
[recall cases](../evals/memory/recall.json).

## Historical profile verification

Verified 2026-10-29: 38 memory-profile checks passed, including all four views,
mixed-scope rejection, byte/fact bounds, TTL clamping, retained history, legacy
definition compatibility, frozen binding validation and denial of private SQL
helpers. The full local suite passed 553 tests, with Ruff, mypy over 49 modules,
host JavaScript syntax, twelve repeated role scenarios and six offline judge
cases. No paid calls are used by that suite. The separate live routing comparison
used typed recall in every arm; it does not compare memory-mode decision quality.

## Historical local verification

Verified 2026-10-28 (Europe/Madrid): the complete suite passed **307 tests**.
Ruff, JavaScript syntax and mypy over 36 source files passed. Tests use real
scoped Postgres identities to deny other orders, stores and roles, direct history
reads, forged sources, untyped fields, stale leases and budget resets. They also
check current-request recall, expiry without older-value resurrection, rejected
old snapshots, concurrent capacity admission and transactional ACK rollback.

A fresh two-order run delivered both meals through 48 events with zero dead
letters and zero model calls. It retained 42 typed revisions and recorded 26
recalled facts; each recalled source matched the decision owner and current order.
Stock invariants and all five replay projections matched. Browser checks covered
readable provenance/expiry, actual recalled values, the legacy 64-order history,
closed raw evidence, zero console errors and no horizontal overflow.
The [local receipt](evidence/typed-memory-local.json) records these counts. This is
a functional/isolation receipt, not a latency or decision-quality benchmark.

The default 64-order city also completed: 1,762 events, zero retries/dead letters
or model calls, 1,791 replay facts and matching projections/invariants. This check
first exposed live-memory pressure from closed supplier requests. The terminal
retention policy above fixed it without raising the 64-entry limit; a regression
test checks that expiry retains history and does not revive older reservations.
The deliberately scarce baseline still delivered seven meals and failed 57 on
supply/deadline constraints, with 21 open physical jobs and three late physical
deliveries retained in its evidence. This memory change does not improve those
business outcomes.

## Enterprise patterns informing the design

- [Google ADK session, state and memory separation](https://adk.dev/sessions/):
  separate a conversation's events and working state from searchable knowledge
  across conversations. Our order trace and private working records address the
  first part; cross-session knowledge remains to be built.
- [Google Agent Platform Memory Bank](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/scale/memory-bank):
  identity-scoped retrieval, background extraction/consolidation, expiry and memory
  revisions are useful reference capabilities. We do not provision this service.
  A scope string alone is not authorization; IAM or database policy must enforce it.
- [LangGraph memory](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/concepts/memory):
  durable thread checkpoints and separately namespaced long-term stores. We use
  database transactions and events rather than importing its graph/checkpointer.
- [OpenAI context engineering with sessions](https://developers.openai.com/cookbook/examples/agents_sdk/session_memory):
  bounded recent turns and structured summaries help control context size. We
  have numeric budgets but do not yet compact or summarize agent conversations.

## Next slices

1. **Broader recall evaluation.** Extend the implemented three-case local
   semantic-recall comparison to more roles and measured model outcomes. Jev ingredient
   search is a separate capability, not a memory search engine. New fact schemas
   need reviewed migrations and compatibility tests, not edits to old records.
2. **Small handoff records.** Queue an explicit brief with the order, current
   commitments, custody, deadline, last verified observation and evidence links.
   Export only approved fields. A courier or supplier should not receive the
   sender's whole memory or another customer's conversation.
3. **Consolidation outside the critical path.** At order closure, derive useful
   facts such as observed supplier delays. Start with local rules. Any optional
   model summary needs its own budget, provenance, validation and expiry; it must
   not edit the agent's instructions or grant capabilities. Raw customer text
   remains untrusted data, including when recalled later.
4. **Publish memory evaluations.** Compare no-memory, typed working records,
   filtered recall and compact summaries on the same seeds. Measure task success,
   stale-fact errors, recovery correctness, retrieval latency, context size and
   model cost when explicitly enabled. Include expired stock, contradicted facts,
   duplicated events, interrupted writes, malicious complaints and cross-role
   retrieval attempts. Require zero unauthorized disclosure or inventory-policy
   violations; publish measured results rather than claiming framework parity.

The typed records and filtered recall are implemented; comparative performance
and decision-quality evaluations remain future work. A vector database or larger
context window by itself would not demonstrate better memory.
docs/AGENT-RUNTIME.md:
# Local agent foundation and optional GCP portability

Original design: 2026-10-23; implementation clarifications: 2026-10-28. Default city
development remains local, without provider calls or cloud credentials. The optional
Cloud Run/Vertex recovery judge has since been implemented and live-verified;
Google ADK and a fully cloud-hosted business runtime remain proposed adapters.
Use [the exact implementation](AGENT-IMPLEMENTATION.md),
[current GCP inventory](GCP-COMPONENTS.md) and
[enterprise decisions](ENTERPRISE-GCP.md) for the current source-reviewed contract.

The inventory implementation is now available: see [implemented foundation](AGENT-FOUNDATION.md)
for actual modules, permissions, budgets and verification. The proposed ADK-specific
shape and example contract below remain future design, not the executable role schema.

## What an agent is in this project

An agent is a versioned identity with a goal, a bounded decision loop, observations,
permitted actions and durable accountability. Its lifecycle is:

claim event -> verify authenticated scope -> commit durable attempt/tool allowance
-> prepare/invoke/save outside effects transaction if enabled -> begin fenced effects transaction -> load
permitted facts/memory -> decide and execute permitted tools -> record outcome,
memory and outgoing events -> commit those effects and ACK atomically.

A prompt or SOUL.md supplies behavioral guidance. It does not provide security,
durability, memory isolation, approvals or cost enforcement. A deterministic policy
and an ADK reasoning policy should both fit the same event and tool contracts, so
the experiment can measure whether model judgment helps.

## Researched Google options (not a deployment choice)

| Option | Documented capability | Project judgment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ADK on Cloud Run | Open-source agent framework with local and cloud deployment. Cloud Run has services for request-driven work, worker pools for continuous queue consumers and jobs for finite tasks. | Deferred portability candidate after local acceptance. Research suggests explicit control over our queue contract and a shared image; jobs, worker pools and services are possible future adapters, not current implementation requirements. |
| Managed Agent Runtime | Managed agent deployment, scaling, security and framework integration. Current docs place it under Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform; ReasoningEngine remains an API resource name for compatibility. | Keep as a deployment adapter option when managed operations justify it. It does not replace business transactions, queue semantics or our scoped memory experiment. |
| Managed Agents API | Config-driven autonomous agents in sandbox environments; launch stage and data-handling terms need review for the chosen feature/version. | Evaluate only on synthetic fixtures first; private Bakiano exports are outside the current approved model data contract. |
| ADK Agent Config | Version-sensitive configuration-based role/workflow assembly. | Preserve our small validated role contract and use a future adapter over tested, pinned ADK APIs; framework configuration is not the durable authorization contract. |

Sources: [ADK overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/build/adk),
[Cloud Run resource choices](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/ai-agents),
[Agent Runtime](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/build/runtime),
[Managed Agents API and restrictions](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/build/managed-agents),
[experimental Agent Config](https://adk.dev/agents/config/).

These links preserve research, not a selected deployment or a dependency of the local
lab. Benchmark the same role/tools against a rules-only baseline locally.
Pin a tested ADK/SDK version and model version in implementation; do not use a moving
latest alias in scored runs. Verify regional availability, quotas and pricing before
deploying. No cloud resources or paid model calls were created by this research.

## Reuse the implementation, specialize the role

Proposed repository shape:

```text
agent_runtime/
  factory.py          # role config -> deterministic or ADK decision policy
  worker.py           # queue lease, deadline, bounded loop, commit/ACK
  context.py          # authoritative reads, redaction, scoped memory retrieval
  tools.py            # fixed tool registry and schema validation
  budgets.py          # durable reservation before inference/tool expense
  telemetry.py        # event/decision/model/tool spans and sanitized records
  transports/         # Postgres first; cloud notification adapter later
config/agents/
  inventory/role.json
  inventory/SOUL.md
  dispatcher/role.json
  dispatcher/SOUL.md
  director/role.json
  director/SOUL.md
config/topologies/    # reporting/approval routes, separate from role behavior
```

These proposed paths describe a future reasoning adapter layout. The implemented
inventory foundation uses `src/delivery/agent_runtime.py`, `agent_access.py` and
`agent_specs.py`, plus the inventory role/soul paths shown above.
Build and validate one shared factory locally, with deterministic policies and scripted
model adapters. ADK is optional behind these contracts; default demos make no provider
calls. ADK packaging and cloud business-worker hosting remain proposed; the bounded
Cloud Run/Vertex judge and its standalone Terraform root are already implemented.
Copy a role configuration and soul file, not the worker implementation. Instantiate
inventory roles with store-specific scope. Configuration is developer-controlled,
immutable during a run, validated at startup and hashed into every decision record.
Event payloads cannot choose a new soul, tools, identity or broader scope.

Example project role contract (illustrative, not directly executable ADK config):

```json
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "role": "inventory",
  "version": "1",
  "soul": "SOUL.md",
  "objective": "Report stock truthfully and propose feasible replenishment",
  "decision_policy": "rules-first-adk-on-exception",
  "scope": {"store_ids": ["store-1"]},
  "accepts": ["basket.requested", "availability.requested", "stock.shortage"],
  "emits": ["inventory.decided", "replenishment.proposed", "approval.requested"],
  "tools": ["inventory.read", "inventory.reserve", "replenishment.propose"],
  "memory": {"namespace": "run/role/store", "retention": "scenario-defined"},
  "model_policy": "budgeted-exception-model-v1",
  "limits": {"model_calls_per_event": 1, "tool_steps_per_event": 6},
  "budget_policy": "inventory-run-budget-v1",
  "output_schema": "inventory-decision-v1",
  "deadline_policy": "inventory-deadlines-v1",
  "escalation_route": "topology.inventory.supervisor"
}
```

Budget/model/deadline references resolve to trusted versioned policies with numeric
caps. The tool list is intersected with server-side policy for the authenticated
principal; editing JSON cannot grant new authority. In a future reasoning adapter,
trusted SOUL text can guide model decisions within that authority. Current local
policies do not interpret SOUL, and the GCP gateway uses its own fixed prompt rather
than the local role SOUL. Neither can raise budgets or remove approval requirements.

Example inventory soul:

> Protect stock accuracy and explain uncertainty. Read authoritative availability
> before making a promise. Separate confirmed units from expected receipts. Prefer
> deterministic tools for stock arithmetic. Propose alternatives only within verified
> compatibility and customer consent. Escalate requests outside your store or authority.

## Local sample data

Target ten daily Bakiano sample dates: 2026-10-14 through 2026-10-23 inclusive.
October 13 through October 23 inclusive would be eleven dates. Keep dated snapshots
local, with source identity, actual observation timestamps, provenance and hashes.
Only label a date observed when authentic source data establishes it; list missing
days explicitly. Never invent historical prices or relabel a current observation as
a past one. Synthetic fallback rows must be clearly marked and cannot fill an
observed-history claim.

## Isolation and data leakage

- Share the container image across roles, but deploy different authority boundaries
  with different workload identities, database roles and tool permissions. Two ADK
  objects in one process do not establish IAM isolation.
- Resolve store/run scope from trusted deployment configuration and authenticated
  tool context. Do not trust a store ID supplied by the model as authorization.
- Give agents narrow projections of catalogue and order facts, not the full Bakiano
  checkout, warehouse account, source credentials or another role's transcript.
- Keep provider credentials in workload identity/secret facilities, never prompts,
  memory documents, event payloads or traces. Avoid downloaded long-lived service
  account keys. Review granted identity defaults rather than assuming no access.
- Separate transient reasoning context, scoped episodes and canonical state. Filter
  memory access before retrieval, not by asking the model to ignore unauthorized hits.
- Treat complaints, product text and retrieved episodes as untrusted data. Enforce
  allowed actions in tools; record injection rejection without propagating secrets.

Google's managed Agent Identity is associated with the deployed runtime resource;
arbitrary role names within one deployment do not automatically get distinct
identities. Agent Gateway provides governance over approved destinations and tools.
These complement, rather than replace, store-level business authorization.
Sources: [Agent Identity](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/scale/runtime/agent-identity),
[Agent Gateway](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/govern/gateways/agent-gateway-overview).

## Queues, state and execution boundaries

Keep Postgres as the authoritative business store and durable event queue initially.
GCP can host it in Cloud SQL, subject to deployment/extension checks. The local Docker
backend remains the offline reference. Current memory uses typed facts and exact
SQL filters. Any future pgvector adapter must be a separately evaluated scoped
memory mode so comparisons do not silently switch memory systems.

For persistent workers, Cloud Run worker pools can consume the existing queue. For
finite experiments, a run-to-completion job can drive the simulation. Do not move
the current API background-task controller unchanged onto a request-billed service.
Durable controller ownership/checkpoints and restart recovery must precede claims
of cloud fault tolerance.

If adopting Pub/Sub later, select and document one transport contract. An outbox
relay may send durable wakeups while Postgres retains priority, simulated due-time
and idempotency semantics. If Pub/Sub becomes the actual transport, add a transactional
inbox/outbox and explicitly reimplement/test these semantics. Do not claim Pub/Sub
natively provides our priority queue or simulation clock.

All role-to-role cooperation stays queued. Do not wire ADK AgentTool, direct agent
transfer, shared conversational state or A2A calls around this ledger. A supervisor
requests another role's work with a correlated event; the result is another event.

ADK trigger endpoints can process Pub/Sub/Eventarc requests, but redelivery creates
another session and default in-memory sessions are ephemeral. Deduplicate with the
business event ID, not an ADK session ID. Pub/Sub exactly-once is regional and pull-only;
it does not establish exactly-once business effects or external model billing.
Sources: [ambient agents](https://adk.dev/runtime/ambient-agents/),
[Pub/Sub delivery guarantees](https://docs.cloud.google.com/pubsub/docs/exactly-once-delivery).

Implemented for the optional judge: model calls run outside worker database
connections. A fenced request snapshots scoped facts, local proposal, recall and
identity. Before dispatch, current context/time/recall and remaining tool slots
are checked; a single-dispatch marker and call/token allowance commit first.
Structured results are saved separately. A fresh effects transaction revalidates
the snapshot before applying domain effects, memory, outgoing events and ACK
atomically. Reclaimed events reuse saved results without another call. An uncertain
dispatch fails closed rather than automatically spending again. Legacy calls
without a compatible durable snapshot are also denied without resend.
See [durable inference](DURABLE-INFERENCE.md). Gateway-wide monetary admission,
supervisor recovery and distributed tracing remain enterprise follow-up work.

## Next implementation gate

Before adding more reasoning roles:

1. Implemented for eight role kinds: strict schema, fixed tools and shared factory;
   deterministic policies are the default and the optional GCP judge is bounded.
2. Real non-superuser tests exercise store/run/role/order/request/attempt isolation;
   twelve local role scenarios now have explicit scores and repeated receipts.
3. Add an ADK reasoning adapter only behind the tested event/tool contracts; keep
   routine city development independent of cloud deployments and inference.
4. Extend adversarial tests for every new model/tool integration; prompts cannot
   grant tools, memory, spending or approval authority, and cooperation stays queued.
5. Replace the in-process controller with durable ownership and checkpoints. Kill
   controller and worker separately and demonstrate local recovery from both.
6. Preserve sample provenance, explicit missing days and the local baseline while
   separately evaluating any paid cloud decision or proposed hosting change.

## Deferred ADK and cloud-worker adapters

The existing standalone Terraform root, keyless Cloud Run judge and start/status/
stop commands are implemented; they do not host the city, business workers or
memory in GCP. ADK, managed agent hosting, cloud business storage and broader
governance remain separate proposed changes. Preserve the shared contracts and
prove reliability/cost gates before adopting them. No deployment or provider call
is required by routine local development or by this documentation review.
docs/ARCHITECTURE-DECISIONS.md:
# Architecture decisions

These records explain the implemented choices reviewed on **2026-10-28** and
when to reconsider them. The local environment supplies reproducible engineering
evidence; it does not establish production scale or superiority over another
agent architecture. [Enterprise GCP](ENTERPRISE-GCP.md) expands the proposed
deployment and governance work.

## 1. Keep the queue and business effects in PostgreSQL

**Choice.** Use addressed events, leases, fencing, priorities, retries and dead
letters beside the domain tables. The worker commits state, memory, decision,
outgoing events and ACK in one effects transaction. Attempt/model reservations
commit separately and survive failure.

**Alternative.** Introduce a message broker as the authoritative work transport.
**Why.** A stock change and its handoff can share a database transaction; a crash
cannot commit consumption while losing its next event. **Trade-off.** Locks and
database capacity constrain execution. Cloud inference now releases its connection
between durable preparation and saved-result application; an uncertain dispatch
fails closed rather than being resent. **Revisit when** measured queue load or independent
consumers justify a broker. Use an outbox/inbox design and failure tests; a broker
does not make external billing exactly once.

Sources: [queue](../src/delivery/queue.py), [runtime](../src/delivery/agent_runtime.py),
[queue boundary tests](../tests/test_agent_queue_boundary.py),
[durable request/result protocol](DURABLE-INFERENCE.md).

## 2. Use rules first, with an optional bounded recovery judge

**Choice.** Fixed policies handle inventory, sourcing, consent, routes and custody.
An explicitly enabled GCP judge may veto a locally computed retry candidate.
**Alternative.** Delegate planning and tool choice to an LLM for every role.
**Why.** Exact stock arithmetic and physical feasibility have executable answers;
default runs remain reproducible without paid inference. **Trade-off.** Fixed
policies cannot interpret an unfamiliar instruction or invent a sourcing strategy.
The model's additional business value remains unmeasured. **Revisit when** an
ambiguous task has an approved evidence contract and a held-out comparison shows
better outcomes within quality, latency and cost gates.

Sources: [supply policy](../src/delivery/supply_policy.py),
[fleet policy](../src/delivery/fleet_policy.py),
[veto/failure tests](../tests/test_cloud_runtime.py).

## 3. Enforce scope outside prompts

**Choice.** Bind each worker's run, namespace and role to its PostgreSQL login;
enforce domain operations through RLS, narrow functions, live leases and budgets.
**Alternative.** Give a shared privileged connection to agents and ask them to
respect their prompt's store/order boundaries. **Why.** Model content, recalled
text and display names cannot grant authority. **Trade-off.** Provisioning and
schema migrations carry complexity. Trusted controller, host and fixed Python
remain outside this boundary; one process holding several connections is not an
OS sandbox. **Revisit when** moving to independently deployed or tenant-facing
workers: add workload identity, process isolation and negative authorization tests.

Sources: [access provisioning](../src/delivery/agent_access.py),
[server-owned authority](../src/delivery/agent_specs.py),
[isolation tests](../tests/test_agent_runtime.py).

## 4. Start with typed memory and explicit sharing

**Choice.** Store versioned observations with server-derived provenance, expiry
and role/order/request/attempt filters. Share approved canonical facts in queued
briefs rather than opening another agent's private memory. **Alternative.** Put
all conversations into shared vector recall by default. **Why.** The current task
needs exact context and auditable stale-fact behavior, not semantic similarity.
**Trade-off.** No cross-order learning, automatic consolidation or semantic recall
exists. TTL controls recall eligibility, not audit deletion. **Revisit when** a
held-out retrieval task demonstrates a gap; compare scoped full-text/vector or
managed memory against this baseline with leakage and latency measurements.

Sources: [typed contracts](../src/delivery/typed_memory.py),
[memory SQL](../sql/migrations/015_typed_memory.sql),
[memory regressions](../tests/test_typed_memory.py).

## 5. Reuse a factory and freeze editable definitions

**Choice.** All supported roles use `LocalAgent`; strict definitions and their
hashes are frozen per run. Supply blueprints allow entity overrides and revision
checks. **Alternative.** Create separate frameworks per role or let instructions
modify capabilities at runtime. **Why.** One execution contract makes permissions,
budgets and evidence consistent. **Trade-off.** SOUL is versioned guidance that
deterministic policies do not interpret; editing it cannot add behavior. The GCP
gateway uses a separate fixed prompt and does not receive local SOUL. **Revisit
when** adding a reasoning adapter: deliberately assemble trusted instructions and
bounded observations, retain prompt versions, and preserve independent enforcement.

Sources: [factory](../src/delivery/agent_runtime.py),
[supply definitions](../src/delivery/supply_models.py),
[definition tests](../tests/test_supply_models.py),
[gateway prompt](../infra/gcp-ai/gateway.py).

## 6. Host the optional judge on Cloud Run

**Choice.** Deploy a stateless container calling Vertex REST, with separate caller
and runtime service accounts. **Alternative.** Managed Agent Runtime, ADK hosting
or GKE. **Why.** A bounded HTTP verdict fits the existing explicit container,
IAM and Terraform lifecycle. **Trade-off.** Managed sessions, memory, agent
identity and governance are not supplied by this design. Network reachability
is public with authenticated invocation. **Revisit when** client requirements
justify managed lifecycle capabilities or different isolation/network controls.
Evaluate the same task and permissions; a framework object alone does not create
a distinct workload identity.

Sources: [Terraform](../infra/gcp-ai/main.tf),
[cloud client](../src/delivery/cloud_ai.py), [component inventory](GCP-COMPONENTS.md).

## 7. Keep routine work local and park billable runtime explicitly

**Choice.** Default providers are disabled. Optional GCP resources belong to a
dedicated Terraform project. Daily stop removes Cloud Run, its invoker binding and
Artifact Registry before unlinking billing; project, APIs and IAM remain.
**Alternative.** Always-on cloud infrastructure or deleting/recreating the entire
project each session. **Why.** Local checks need no model account, while retained
identity/project ownership avoids repeated setup. **Trade-off.** Retention and
shutdown need explicit accounting. Six per-run model calls and token reservations
do not create a project-wide dollar cap. **Revisit when** a client needs persistent
services, backups or multi-caller inference; add cost admission and declared
retention/containment ownership.

Sources: [local Compose](../compose.yaml), [lifecycle helper](../scripts/gcp_demo.py),
[lifecycle tests](../tests/test_gcp_demo_commands.py), [operations](GCP-AI.md).

## 8. Publish measured receipts before architecture rankings

**Choice.** Keep source-linked tests, fixed scenario criteria, repeat hashes,
business replay and explicit freshness. **Alternative.** Rank architectures or
models from a convincing animation or one successful run. **Why.** A safe rejection
can be correct; scores require declared expectations and complete measurements.
**Trade-off.** The battery covers development regressions, not generalization,
production SLOs or causal business uplift. **Revisit when** comparing flat,
hierarchical or planner/executor designs: freeze paired incidents, hold out case
families, repeat trials and publish quality, latency, cost and failure outcomes.

Sources: [scenario evaluator](../src/delivery/scenario_evals.py),
[receipt validation](../src/delivery/scenario_report.py),
[reporting tests](../tests/test_scenario_evals.py), [evidence guide](CAPABILITY-EVIDENCE.md).
docs/ARCHITECTURE-OBSERVABILITY.md:
# Observability architecture

Tracing and BigQuery analytics are independent opt-ins. Both are disabled by
default. Setting a project ID alone does not discover credentials or send data.
Model inference has its existing, separate admission and cost controls.

## Trace flow

This diagram follows an order through the API, durable queue, agents and tools:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    API["FastAPI request"] --> Publish["Order publish span"]
    Publish --> Queue[("Postgres queue: W3C parent")]
    Queue --> Worker["Leased worker span"]
    Worker --> Agent["Agent / ADK model span"]
    Agent --> Tool["Scoped tool span"]
    Tool --> Redis["Redis command span"]
    Tool --> Queue
    Worker --> Terminal["Committed terminal outcome"]
    API & Publish & Worker & Agent & Tool & Redis --> Filter["Allowlist and bounded export"]
    Filter --> Local["Console or local OTLP"]
    Filter --> Cloud["Cloud Trace when project is configured"]
    Filter --> Batch["Optional bounded BigQuery batch writer"]
    Terminal --> Batch
    Eval["Eval receipt: cases and repetitions"] --> Batch
    Batch --> BQ[("mds_analytics: traces, agent_steps, orders, eval_runs")]
```

An order's trace
ID is derived from its run ID and canonical queue trace key. Reusing an order key
in another run creates a different trace. Migration 027 extends the original
telemetry migration and supports both previously shipped branch schemas. It
persists W3C parents, copies them to SQL-produced descendants and fences worker
updates with the existing lease. Trace context confers no queue authority.

FastAPI and Redis use OpenTelemetry instrumentors. Queue processing, scoped
agent/tool execution and ADK model calls add explicit spans. Agent/tool names,
run/order IDs, attempts, model usage and estimated USD cost are structured
attributes. Model spans carry cost once; outer agent/tool spans do not duplicate
it. Missing usage remains unknown. Costs are estimates, not a billing statement.

The exporter strips request bodies, tool arguments, Redis command arguments,
exception messages and stack traces. The application's private provider does not
enable ADK's raw prompt/response tracing. Existing private Postgres evidence is
unchanged. Span names and the documented operational attributes are exported;
use synthetic, non-sensitive order IDs.

## Local tracing

With dependencies installed, enable console export in the process you want to
inspect:

```bash
MDS_TELEMETRY_ENABLED=1 python3 -m delivery.cli lab-demo
```

For a local OTLP HTTP collector, leave `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` unset and set
`OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:4318`. The traces-specific
`OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT` is also supported. Inside Docker, use the
collector's container-network address. Console export is the fallback when no
project or OTLP endpoint is configured. `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME` defaults to
`madrid-delivery-sim`.

Compose forwards the two feature flags, project ID and generic OTLP endpoint
from the host or `.env`. It does not mount credentials. For example:

```bash
docker compose run --rm -e MDS_TELEMETRY_ENABLED=1 app delivery lab-demo
```

## Google Cloud setup

In the existing `infra/gcp-ai` Terraform root, opt into `enable_cloud_trace=true`
and/or `enable_analytics=true` with `enable_billing=true`. Review a plan before
applying it. These flags provision infrastructure; they do not enable application
exports. No cloud deployment or paid call is required to test this implementation.

If either feature branch was previously applied, follow the
[Terraform state migration notes](../infra/gcp-ai/STATE-MIGRATION.md) before
planning. Receipt exports retain the separate `delivery_analytics` dataset;
streaming telemetry uses `mds_analytics`. The migration notes prevent an existing
dataset from being mistaken for the other one.

The module creates an `observability-writer` identity for local offline/eval
exporters. Native ADK keeps its `restaurant-adk` credentials and the Cloud Run
judge keeps `judgement-runtime`; the enabled Terraform flags also grant these
existing producer identities the same scoped export permissions. The invocation-only
`judgement-caller` identity receives no analytics access. Trace access uses
`roles/cloudtrace.agent`. Analytics uses a custom append-only role scoped to the
dataset; query, export, table creation and deletion permissions are not granted
to the application. Use attached credentials in Google Cloud or keyless service
account impersonation. Provision reader/query access separately for analysts.
The module creates no service-account keys.

In the application process, set:

```bash
export GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT=your-project-id
export MDS_TELEMETRY_ENABLED=1
export MDS_BIGQUERY_ENABLED=1
```

When tracing is enabled and the project is set, Cloud Trace takes precedence over
the local exporters. BigQuery alone enables the spans needed for analytics without
also exporting to Cloud Trace. Missing credentials or an exporter outage is logged
with a sanitized category and does not change task outcomes.

## Analytics tables and saved queries

Terraform creates `mds_analytics` in `EU` by default. Its four tables use daily
`observed_at` partitions, require partition filters and cluster on `agent`.
Retention defaults to 90 days and is configurable from 1 to 365 days. The dataset
location is immutable after creation. Runtime `MDS_BIGQUERY_DATASET` can target a
separately provisioned dataset with the same schema.

| Table | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| `traces` | Sanitized span IDs, parents, names, status and duration |
| `agent_steps` | Agent/model/tool spans, usage, cost and available success status |
| `orders` | Observed terminal outcomes, deduplicated by run-scoped trace and order |
| `eval_runs` | One row per case, arm and repetition, including failures and omissions |

Each completed span has its own stable insertion ID. Re-exporting that span reuses
the same ID and payload; later terminal acknowledgements have distinct IDs. SQL
selects the earliest observed terminal per trace before counting successful orders.

The writer batches up to 100 rows with a two-second flush interval and a
10,000-row queue. Transient failures retry up to three attempts with stable row
IDs. Requests have a five-second timeout. A bounded shutdown drains pending rows;
overflow and exhausted/permanent failures increment dropped counters and log
sanitized warnings. `writer.counters` exposes accepted, inserted, retried, dropped
and pending counts. Monitor drops and export failures before trusting completeness.

This buffer is in memory: a process crash can lose queued telemetry. Streaming
insert IDs offer best-effort deduplication, not exactly-once storage. Business
receipts remain authoritative in Postgres and local artifacts. The saved queries
deduplicate before aggregating and measure observed evidence:

- [Cost per successful task by agent](../sql/analytics/cost_per_successful_task.sql)
  includes failed/incomplete task cost and returns unknown when model cost is
  missing. It joins by trace ID so repeated order keys cannot merge separate runs.
- [p95 tool latency](../sql/analytics/p95_tool_latency.sql) reports wall-clock
  tool duration and sample counts, including failures.
- [Evaluation pass^k trend](../sql/analytics/eval_pass_power_k_trend.sql) reports
  the fraction of complete case groups passing every repetition, separated by
  evaluation mode, fixture, revision and k. Incomplete groups are reported
  separately and cannot count as successful evidence.

Replace `PROJECT_ID` in each GoogleSQL file and bind `start_time` and `end_time`
as timestamp query parameters. Use a query identity with an explicit scan budget.
Time windows and retention limit the evidence available to these queries. Order
latency uses the earliest observed terminal acknowledgement, not simulated minutes
or a guaranteed exact instant of physical delivery.

Both `scripts/eval_agents.py` and `scripts/eval_cloud_judge.py` export after writing
their local receipt when analytics is enabled. Fresh ADK evaluation attempts retain
their arm, case, repetition and evaluation mode; stored golden assertions are not
counted as new model attempts. The scenario runner retains
`mode=local-deterministic`: its repeated runs test reproducibility, not independent
LLM reliability. Changed source or changed repeat inputs cannot export a green
result. Unknown model costs remain null. Analytics failures never change
the evaluator's exit code or overwrite its local receipt.

## Retention and verification

Table deletion protection defaults on. Export required evidence, explicitly apply
`analytics_deletion_protection=false`, then review a separate opt-out plan before
removing analytics. The ordinary GCP demo stop command refuses to park a project
that still has observability configured or retained analytics, rather than silently
delete data or leave an assumed-free project with storage. Inspect its status and
the Terraform plan before changing billing.

Fake-client/exporter tests cover disabled mode, propagation, privacy, partial
failures and shutdown. The regular integration suite exercises real Postgres
leases and offline ADK calls; Terraform tests use a mocked provider. No GCP
credentials are needed for these checks:

```bash
python3 -m pytest -q tests/test_telemetry.py tests/test_analytics.py tests/test_eval_analytics.py
terraform -chdir=infra/gcp-ai init -backend=false
terraform -chdir=infra/gcp-ai validate
terraform -chdir=infra/gcp-ai test
```

Implementation references, reviewed 2026-10-29:
[OpenTelemetry propagation](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/languages/python/propagation/),
[Google Cloud Trace instrumentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/trace/docs/setup),
[Cloud Trace exporter](https://google-cloud-opentelemetry.readthedocs.io/en/stable/cloud_trace/cloud_trace.html),
[BigQuery streaming error and deduplication behavior](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/streaming-data-into-bigquery),
and [BigQuery client API](https://cloud.google.com/python/docs/reference/bigquery/latest/google.cloud.bigquery.client.Client).
docs/ARCHITECTURE-OVERVIEW.md:
# Architecture overview

This project is a local engineering environment for studying bounded agent work:
ingredient sourcing, stock reservations, consent, courier assignment, physical
delivery and recovery. Its reusable runtime combines authenticated Python workers
with PostgreSQL transactions. Most decisions use fixed rules. A separately enabled
GCP recovery judge complements Google ADK restaurant and customer-service adapters.
Both ADK roles have scripted, zero-network models for CI. The dispatcher and
customer service are discoverable over local A2A; optional OTel spans and
BigQuery exports connect decisions to operational evidence.

This chapter describes source reviewed on **2026-10-29**. It does not report a new
deployment or a current cloud inventory. Read [capability evidence](CAPABILITY-EVIDENCE.md)
for measured limits and [architecture decisions](ARCHITECTURE-DECISIONS.md) for
the alternatives behind these choices.

## Three boundaries

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph Local["Local Docker environment"]
        Operator["Operator UI and trusted controller"]
        World["Synthetic city and physical world engine"]
        Workers["Scoped Python LocalAgent workers"]
        DB[("PostgreSQL: domain state, queue, memory, budgets and audit")]
        Client["Optional CloudJudge client"]
        Operator --> Workers
        Operator --> World
        World <--> DB
        Workers <--> DB
        Workers -->|"Explicit GCP judge mode"| Client
    end
    subgraph Cloud["Optional Terraform-owned GCP resources"]
        IAM["Cloud Run IAM: caller identity"]
        Gateway["Cloud Run judgement container"]
        Model["Google publisher model through Vertex REST"]
        Image["Artifact Registry: immutable image digest"]
        Logs["Platform logs and structured gateway stdout"]
        IAM --> Gateway
        Image -.-> Gateway
        Gateway -->|"Runtime service account ADC"| Model
        Gateway --> Logs
    end
    Client -->|"HTTPS and audience-bound ID token"| IAM
    Gateway -->|"Validated verdict and usage"| Client
```

The **city boundary** owns virtual time, directed roads, congestion, courier
movement and recorded arrival. Agents request permitted transitions; they cannot
manufacture physical arrival. The **agent boundary** owns scoped observations,
approved tools, leased work and bounded recall. PostgreSQL is the authority for
stock, consent, custody and execution. Redis supports the local baseline but is
not the authoritative agent transport.

The **cloud boundary** accepts a bounded numeric recovery proposal and returns an
approve/deny verdict. It has no simulation database connection or execution tools.
Caller and runtime service accounts have separate duties. Cloud Run is reachable
over the public network with IAM-authenticated invocation; the Terraform module
does not provide private ingress. Cloud SQL, Pub/Sub, GKE, managed Agent
Runtime and Memory Bank are not deployed. Google ADK runs as a local Python
library; optional Cloud Trace and BigQuery resources are declared but parked.
See the [Google stack guide](GOOGLE-STACK.md) and
[exact GCP inventory](GCP-COMPONENTS.md).

## What an agent actually is

`create_agent` produces the same frozen `LocalAgent` class for inventory,
fulfillment, dispatch, couriers, the recovery judge and supply entities. Its
inputs resolve to an authenticated scope, validated `RoleSpec`, definition hash
and restricted database connection. The public loop is `claim()` followed by
`process(event)`. Role-specific policies decide through `ScopedTools`; the factory
does not generate a new program for each fictional participant.

A trusted controller provisions the login and freezes the definition. SQL derives
scope from the authenticated database identity. Server-owned authority limits
tools, accepted topics and recipients. Editable names and SOUL text describe the
role; current deterministic policies do not interpret SOUL. Business settings
such as stock, opening hours, latency and numeric limits have implemented effects.
New roles still require code, database permissions and tests. The complete
[agent construction walkthrough](AGENT-IMPLEMENTATION.md) follows these steps.

For one event, an attempt/tool reservation commits first. The effects transaction
then validates the lease and authoritative payload, reads domain state and typed
recall, executes allowed actions, records the decision and outgoing events, and
ACKs. Those effects commit together or roll back together. Durable reservations
survive failure. This protects business effects without promising exactly-once
external inference or billing. Sources: [runtime](../src/delivery/agent_runtime.py),
[queue](../src/delivery/queue.py), [identity provisioning](../src/delivery/agent_access.py).

## Follow one household pizza request

This is a representative path with a pantry shortage, not a promise that every
seed follows it. Role handoffs use typed queued events; notes and self-steps
describe domain work.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant H as Household agent
    participant R as Restaurant agent
    participant M as Market agent
    participant D as Dispatcher
    participant C as Courier agent
    participant W as Physical world
    H->>R: household.call for pizza
    R->>M: market.request for missing ingredient
    Note over M: Reserve own stock or forward to an unvisited market
    M->>R: ingredient.arrived after transfer
    Note over H,R: A replacement requires explicit household approval
    Note over R: Cook only from arrived, reserved ingredients
    R->>D: basket.ready
    D->>C: courier.briefed
    C->>D: courier.accepted
    W->>D: delivery.arrived after road traversal
    D->>D: dispatch.complete records delivered status
    H->>H: meal.delivery checks canonical job status
```

The restaurant first checks menu, availability and pantry. Markets reserve
unreserved quantities atomically, or forward shortages through a bounded visited
list. A promised ingredient is unusable until arrival commits. A substitution
must satisfy the fixed rules, household exclusions and recorded consent before
cooking consumes the physical allocations once.

Cooking creates a delivery job and a dispatcher handoff. The courier must accept
its own briefing before departure; the world advances it along directed edges.
Ingredient transfer uses scheduled transitions rather than a separate moving
supplier vehicle. The restaurant-to-courier handoff **is implemented**; it is
covered by [delivery-fact regressions](../tests/test_supply_delivery_facts.py).

## Observability trace flow

Observability is disabled by default. One run-scoped order trace continues across
durable queue handoffs and lease retries. Explicit agent, ADK model and tool spans
record names, usage and estimated cost; FastAPI and Redis use OpenTelemetry
instrumentors. Exporters remove payloads and exception text before sending data.

The [Mermaid trace-flow diagram](ARCHITECTURE-OBSERVABILITY.md#trace-flow) follows
the API, persisted queue context, agent/tool spans and both export paths.

Trace and analytics flags are independent. Analytics outages do not change task
outcomes; Postgres and local receipts remain authoritative. The four BigQuery
tables have daily partitions, agent clustering and bounded retention. Saved SQL
deduplicates streaming rows before calculating cost per successful task, p95 tool
latency and eval pass^k trends. See [setup, privacy, reporting limits and
retention](ARCHITECTURE-OBSERVABILITY.md).

## Distinct workspaces and reading paths

The [restaurant workflow](RESTAURANT-SUPPLY.md) starts with household meal demand,
sourcing and consent, then reuses fleet delivery. The [delivery lab](FLEET-RECOVERY.md)
starts with stocked baskets and concentrates on fulfillment, contention, traffic,
dropouts and checkpoint recovery. They share infrastructure and some roles, but
their seeded scenarios and success criteria differ. The [inventory lab](AGENT-FOUNDATION.md)
isolates last-unit contention, delayed supply and worker crashes.

For a demonstration, open one restaurant order and inspect its call, ingredient
requests, actual memory revisions, queue lineage, cooking and physical handoff.
Then use a delivery-lab failure to inspect custody and the judge's limited
authority. Compare those observations with [local scenario evaluations](AGENT-EVALS.md).

For implementation, continue through [agent internals](AGENT-IMPLEMENTATION.md),
[memory](AGENT-MEMORY.md) and [GCP components](GCP-COMPONENTS.md). For a client or
interview discussion, use the [decision records](ARCHITECTURE-DECISIONS.md) and
[enterprise roadmap](ENTERPRISE-GCP.md). [Durable inference](DURABLE-INFERENCE.md)
now saves requests/results and invokes outside SQL connections, with local crash
verification. Controller recovery, workload identity, retention and measured
production release gates remain proposed work.
docs/CAPABILITY-EVIDENCE.md:
# Capability evidence

The six goals below connect the architecture to executable proof and its limits.
Source review is dated **2026-10-28**. The dated
[implementation review](AGENT-IMPLEMENTATION.md) records **392 passing tests**.
The role battery declares **12 fixed scenarios and 49 criteria**, with matching
outcomes across two seed-731 repetitions. These are historical development results,
not a current service-health statement or a new test run performed by reading
this chapter. The earlier [local receipt](evidence/local-health.json) records a
different snapshot of 353 tests; it is not the receipt for the 392-test result.
See the [scenario receipt](evidence/agent-scenarios-local.json) and
[evaluation contract](AGENT-EVALS.md).

Tests exercise narrower guarantees than their headlines suggest. Follow the
linked assertions, distinguish successful rejection from business success, and
use the running health view for current source/freshness information.

## 1. Queue resilience

**Goal:** agents must cooperate through durable work and recover safely from
duplicates, contention, stale workers and failure.

**Implemented proof:** the [queue](../src/delivery/queue.py) and
[capability migration](../sql/migrations/014_queue_capability.sql) provide addressed
claims, due times, priority, lease fencing, retries/backoff, deduplication and dead
letters. [Queue tests](../tests/test_queue.py) exercise concurrent claims, rollback,
retry and replay. [Agent boundary tests](../tests/test_agent_queue_boundary.py)
reject raw mutation, forged publication and stale ACKs; they recheck deadlines
after lock waits and verify authoritative payload reload. The fixed battery
includes a real worker-process crash before acknowledgement.

**Limit:** domain effects, memory, decision, outbox and ACK are atomic in the fixed
worker. This does not promise exactly-once inference or billing. Sustained
throughput/backpressure, durable controller restart and orphan-login recovery
remain unmeasured or unfinished. The optional judge now invokes outside database
connections, reuses saved results, and fails closed on uncertain abandoned calls.
[Real process-crash tests](../tests/test_inference_crash_recovery.py) verify those
boundaries without paid inference. [Implementation details](DURABLE-INFERENCE.md).

## 2. Hierarchy, coordination and authority

**Goal:** give cooperating roles different responsibilities and prevent one role
from overruling another's business authority.

**Implemented proof:** the [authority contract](../src/delivery/agent_specs.py)
defines each role's tools and topics. A dispatcher assigns work, a courier accepts
its own brief, a judge reviews recovery, and domain commands independently enforce
consent, stock and custody. [Fleet tests](../tests/test_fleet_recovery.py) cover two
dispatchers competing for one bike, cross-courier denial, mandatory judgement and
checkpoint handoff. [Delivery tests](../tests/test_delivery_flow.py) reject
cross-domain commands and invented physical arrival. A judge's verdict cannot
manufacture a route or move a parcel.

**Limit:** role coordination and approval gates are implemented; a generic
hierarchical planner is not. Flat, hierarchical and planner/executor architecture
comparisons are **not implemented**. Counting roles or showing a handoff does not
measure the value of a hierarchy. The host, operator and fixed policies remain
trusted. [Fleet workflow](FLEET-RECOVERY.md).

## 3. Shared memory without unrestricted access

**Goal:** preserve relevant knowledge across handoffs while preventing unrelated
orders, roles and customers from leaking into recall.

**Implemented proof:** [typed memory](../src/delivery/typed_memory.py) stores
validated observations, server-derived provenance and append-only revisions.
Recall derives context from the current authenticated lease. Approved canonical
custody facts are exported in an assignment brief; another agent's private memory
is not shared. [Memory tests](../tests/test_typed_memory.py) cover source forgery,
current-order isolation, concurrent capacity, expiry and suppression of older
