# Multi-basket fleet and judged recovery

The fixed `delivery delivery-demo` runs the local 32×32 synthetic scenario below.
The grid UI is retired; [configurable running-city sessions](RUNNING-CITY.md) remain
as backend regressions, with saved fixed runs inspectable through the delivery API.
Existing saved 10×10 runs and the separate `/lab` inventory
crash/replenishment exercise retain their earlier behavior.

The expanded city has 1,024 nodes, 3,968 directed adjacent roads and 12 establishments:
six supermarkets, three retail stores and three pharmacies. Pharmacy catalogue
rows are simulated hygiene goods. They contain no patient, prescription or medical
decision data. Opening inventory is one or two units per stocked product.

## What the seeded scenario demonstrates

Seven one-item basket requests compete for stock and four bike couriers. Three
couriers start online; the fourth becomes available as a replacement at simulation
second 180. Two baskets compete for the same last unit, so one is rejected. Six
parcels are picked exactly once.

Persistent seeded congestion doubles every directed road's traversal time.
Route validation and physical motion use the same per-edge durations. At second
180 two couriers suffer simulated mechanical failures. Each parcel stays at the
last reached safe checkpoint. A replacement must travel there and collect it;
the system never returns it to a store or consumes another stock unit.

For seed 42, the judge approves recovery of `delivery-a` and denies `delivery-b`,
whose deliberately tight delivery window has already expired. The approved parcel
receives attempt two and a new courier. The final result is five delivered baskets,
one abandoned parcel held at its checkpoint and one rejected stock request.
Abandoned is an explicit failure outcome, not a successful delivery or vanished stock.

## The call is a queued briefing

This demo simulates the call with a scoped queued message. It makes no telephone,
voice-provider or model calls. Dispatch sends `courier.briefed`; the selected courier
agent reads its current briefing and sends `courier.accepted`. Physical departure
cannot precede acknowledgement. If acknowledgement is delayed, departure, pickup
and arrival times move together rather than inventing travel during that delay.

Recovery follows this queue and physical-custody boundary. The fixed scenario
uses local rules. A separately enabled judge can consume a saved provider verdict
through the [durable inference protocol](DURABLE-INFERENCE.md); the same execution
gates remain in force.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph Review["01 / Judge review"]
        Failure["World failure: parcel retained at safe checkpoint"]
        Candidate["Scoped judge computes local courier and route candidate"]
        Verdict["Local rules or saved optional provider verdict; SQL persists bounded review"]
        Failure -->|"Queued delivery.failed"| Candidate
        Candidate --> Verdict
    end
    subgraph Decision["02 / Dispatcher decision"]
        Apply["Apply matching current-attempt review"]
        Held["Denied: abandoned; parcel stays at checkpoint"]
        Retry["Queued dispatch.retry; wait if fleet is busy"]
        Gate["Fresh SQL checks: approved review, free online courier, route, deadline and retry limits"]
        Apply -->|"Denied"| Held
        Apply -->|"Approved"| Retry
        Retry --> Gate
    end
    subgraph Movement["03 / Physical handoff"]
        Assign["Atomic new attempt, courier assignment and scoped briefing"]
        Accept["Queued courier.briefed and courier.accepted before departure"]
        Travel["Collect same parcel at checkpoint; world records delivery.arrived"]
        Complete["Dispatcher confirms delivery.completed"]
        Assign --> Accept --> Travel --> Complete
    end
    Verdict -->|"Queued recovery.reviewed"| Apply
    Gate -->|"All checks pass"| Assign
```

All role-to-role handoffs use the durable event queue. A self-queued dispatch retry
waits when all online couriers are busy. No role directly calls another role.
The trusted scheduler activates only the appropriate authenticated worker; it does
not pass the operator snapshot into an agent.

## Relevant memory without sharing private memory

A recovery brief is an immutable, run/basket/attempt-scoped export of canonical
facts: objective, custody checkpoint, customer node, prior courier/attempt, failure
reason, source event references, judge verdict, deadline and route. It contains
neither product/price information nor another agent's private episodes, soul or
transcript. The selected courier can read its own current brief; another courier
cannot retrieve or accept it. Old attempt messages cannot mutate the replacement
attempt.

Private expiring agent memory remains in its existing authenticated namespace.
Shared briefs, incidents and reviews are separate operator-owned records accessed
through narrow role projections. An exported brief does not grant access to the
source event bodies or the source agent's memory.

## Judge and permission gates

The judge is a deterministic operational role, distinct from a future external eval
scorer. It sees the failed logistics job, current custody, available online couriers
and traffic-adjusted roads. It cannot inspect stock or product data, assign couriers,
move parcels or confirm delivery.

The database independently recomputes the proposed route. A retry needs an online
free courier, a matching current-attempt review, enough remaining deadline, fewer
than two total attempts, and at most 100 simulated route-minutes. Dispatch rechecks
these limits at assignment time. A prompt or forged verdict event cannot replace
the persisted review. Route-minutes are a synthetic retry-cost proxy, not money.

Thirty independently scoped logins cover 12 inventory roles, 12 fulfillment roles,
four courier roles, one dispatcher and one judge. Courier and judge logins cannot
read raw operational tables or execute another role's commands. Legacy command entry points cannot be called by agents to bypass the expanded checks. The host, fixed Python policy
code and operator interface remain trusted; arbitrary agent-written Python is not
sandboxed by these database boundaries.

Dispatcher limits are explicitly configured at 150 attempts and 1,200 reserved
tool slots for the larger scenario. Other role defaults remain 100 attempts and
400 slots. The aggregate cap remains 500 attempts and 2,000 slots; model caps remain
zero. Durable reservations are not refunded on crashes or replayed attempts.

## Evidence and current limits

The inspector exposes current routes, online/offline fleet state, traffic and dropout
incidents, judge reasons, custody briefs, attempt history, budgets and event lineage.
Arrival/collection timeline entries come from recorded physical observations, not
obsolete planned timestamps. Evidence exports retain checkpoints and conserved stock.

The full Linux suite passes **86 tests**, Ruff and mypy. Chrome checks pass for
city counts, both judge verdicts, custody briefing provenance, evidence download,
completed-run reload and desktop/mobile layout.

Verification covers two independent dispatcher workers claiming different queued
jobs while competing for one online bike: one assigns, the other defers. It also
covers cross-courier briefing denial, cross-role command denial, missing-review
denial, acknowledgement timing, stock conservation, custody tracking and both judge
outcomes. Existing Madrid, inventory crash and legacy delivery tests remain part
of the regression suite.

Freshly published events are immediately wall-clock eligible; simulation due time
still controls scheduling. Wall-clock retry backoff and leases remain enforced.
This prevents transaction timestamps or clock adjustments from making fresh events
temporarily invisible and changing a seeded run's initial assignments.

Still deferred for this fixed scenario: real voice calls, live traffic, arbitrary incidents,
road-capacity queues, cargo/energy constraints, cancellation/returns, controller
restart recovery, full replay and published multi-seed architecture comparisons.
docs/GCP-AI.md:
# Optional GCP judgement gateway

Architecture reading order: [exact agent implementation](AGENT-IMPLEMENTATION.md),
[Terraform/GCP component inventory](GCP-COMPONENTS.md), then
[enterprise decisions and gaps](ENTERPRISE-GCP.md). This document is the operations
runbook. The gateway evidence below retains its 2026-10-25 verification; native
ADK inference was additionally verified and parked on 2026-10-29. This is not a
fresh status query on each documentation update. "Private" means IAM-authenticated
invocation here; the current service has network-reachable ingress.

The local city works without GCP. The optional switch sends only a bounded retry judgement to a private Cloud Run gateway using Vertex AI. Inventory, fulfillment, dispatch, couriers, movement, custody and SQL policy enforcement remain local and deterministic. This is a hosted judgement role, not a hosted fleet. A live deployment and UI verification were completed on 2026-10-24, followed by verified teardown on 2026-10-25. The project was restored on 2026-10-25 and is parked with billing disabled. The cloud demo is currently off; see [verification](GCP-VERIFICATION.md).

`infra/gcp-ai` is a standalone Terraform root with its own local state. It owns
one persistent, dedicated project, with optional runtime infrastructure. It has no
Scrapmarket dependencies. Never import a shared project or reuse another root's
state. The restored simulation project is imported into its original state.
Project deletion is blocked by both `deletion_policy = "PREVENT"` and
`lifecycle.prevent_destroy`. Keep private variables, plans and state out of Git.

## Daily commands

For native ADK restaurant inference, use `make gcp-vertex-start` followed by
`make demo-adk-vertex`, then `make gcp-stop`. This inference-only path retains a
dedicated `restaurant-adk` service account and enables billing without creating
the gateway or image repository. Only the one-shot local worker receives temporary
impersonated ADC and the ignored Jev credential; the city UI remains offline.
See [restaurant comparison and exact spending limits](ADK-RESTAURANT.md).

From the repository root (Python 3.12+ with only its standard library):

```bash
python3 scripts/gcp_demo.py start
python3 scripts/gcp_demo.py status
python3 scripts/gcp_demo.py stop
```

`make gcp-start`, `make gcp-status` and `make gcp-stop` are equivalent aliases.
The city, homes, stores, stock, orders, queues, roles, memory and rules run locally
in Docker. Building the city and testing deterministic agent/event behavior
requires no GCP deployment or inference. Leave the project parked for that work.

`start` explicitly links billing, creates the image repository, builds/pushes the
small gateway image locally, deploys its immutable digest and reconnects the
local app with a read-only ADC mount. It makes GCP AI available in Configure;
it does not select it or change saved runs. Startup itself makes no model calls.
Image storage and Cloud Run usage can incur charges while enabled. Model charges
begin only when an explicitly cloud-enabled run asks the recovery judge for a
decision. Every stock reservation, route movement and queue event remains local.
Use traces to compare local rules against those selected model decisions.

`stop` resets the app to local mode first, deletes the gateway and stored images
with billing still linked, then unlinks billing. Project, APIs, service accounts,
custom role and free IAM bindings remain. Repeated stop on a parked project does
not relink billing. A deletion failure prevents billing unlinking so cleanup can
be retried. A local app reset failure is reported after attempting cloud cleanup.

`status` reads project lifecycle, billing, actual Cloud Run services, Terraform
runtime resources and local provider availability. With billing enabled it also
lists repositories; otherwise that check is explicitly unavailable. It makes no
model calls and never enables billing to answer a status request. A parked result
is not a billing invoice and does not erase earlier charges.

Prerequisites: gcloud/Terraform/Docker on PATH, Docker running, existing protected
project/IAM state in this root, the ignored `infra/gcp-ai/deploy.auto.tfvars.json`,
and local ADC (`gcloud auth application-default login`). The CLI reads the selected
project/region from that private file. `GCP_ADC_DIRECTORY` can override the usual
local ADC directory; no keys are downloaded. Commands work from any working
directory when invoked with the script's path. Use `APP_PORT` if not 8010.

Commands validate saved plans before applying: foundation changes, replacements,
unexpected resources and another project's runtime are rejected. Desired flags
are saved only after successful apply to the ignored
`zz-demo.auto.tfvars.json`, which overrides the bootstrap values on future plans.
Saved plans remain ignored. Start/stop share a lock; if a process is forcibly
terminated, inspect status and confirm it has stopped before removing
`infra/gcp-ai/.demo-command.lock`. If startup fails after creating resources,
inspect status and run stop. Neither command runs a model evaluation automatically.

## Manual bootstrap (first setup or troubleshooting)

An operator needs project creation and billing-link permissions, Terraform, gcloud and Docker. Select a supported model and Vertex location explicitly; no model or region is assumed. Set `project_id`, `billing_account`, `region`, `vertex_region`, `vertex_model`, and optionally one of `org_id` or `folder_id` in a private tfvars file. Billing, runtime infrastructure and the gateway all default off. Terraform 1.7+ is needed for the mocked lifecycle tests.

1. From `infra/gcp-ai`, run `terraform init`, review `terraform plan`, then `terraform apply`. With all enable flags false this keeps the protected project, six API registrations, both keyless service accounts, the prediction-only custom role and scoped IAM bindings. Set `invoker_members` to explicit operators in the private variables to configure keyless caller impersonation. To bootstrap the repository, set `enable_billing=true`, `enable_runtime=true`, `enable_gateway=false`, review and apply again. This links billing and creates the image repository without Cloud Run; existing identities are reused.
2. From the repository root, build `infra/gcp-ai/Dockerfile` and push the image to the `image_repository` output using an operator's authenticated Docker registry login. For example, `docker build -f infra/gcp-ai/Dockerfile -t REGION-docker.pkg.dev/PROJECT/judgement/gateway:VERSION .` then `docker push` that same tag. Prefer its immutable digest for `gateway_image`. The image must be this gateway, not an arbitrary server.
3. Set `enable_gateway=true`, `gateway_image` to that image, and `invoker_members` to explicit operator principals such as `user:you@example.com`. Review and apply again. There is no `allUsers` binding. Terraform retains the dedicated keyless caller service account and grants only listed operators permission to mint its tokens.
4. Set the server environment variable `DELIVERY_GCP_AI_ENDPOINT` to the `gateway_url` output and select GCP AI mode in the city configuration. The mode is frozen per session. Local mode remains the default. Changing settings affects new sessions only.

Runtime authentication uses Application Default Credentials and an audience-bound Cloud Run ID token. Run `gcloud auth application-default login` locally, then set `DELIVERY_GCP_AI_CALLER_SERVICE_ACCOUNT` to the `caller_service_account` Terraform output. The adapter uses your ADC to impersonate that account and mint an ID token without a downloaded key. Terraform grants listed operators `roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator` only on this caller account and grants that account `roles/run.invoker` only on the gateway. On Cloud Run, attached credentials can supply tokens directly when attached to the authorized caller account. Never use service-account key files or API keys. The gateway runtime receives a project-owned custom role containing only `aiplatform.endpoints.predict` in this dedicated project. Both service accounts, the custom role and their identity-level IAM bindings are owned by this root and retained during routine shutdown. The Cloud Run invocation binding belongs to the deleted service and is recreated with it. Operator identities outside the project are not deleted.

## Contract and limits

`CloudJudge(endpoint).review(context, memory, candidate=proposal)` returns `Judgment`: `decision` is exactly `approve_retry` or `deny_retry`, with a short `reason`, configured `model`, and input/output token counts. The caller reserves its durable model budget **before** invoking this adapter, records the decision, and denies on any authentication, transport, validation or budget error. The caller may approve only its already computed candidate; SQL independently checks deadline, retry and custody invariants.

Only numeric allowlisted job facts, numeric candidate summary (`estimated_seconds`, `remaining_seconds`, `route_nodes`) and memory entry count leave the local application. The gateway adds a reviewed, synthetic seven-meal supermarket snapshot as read-only business reference. Full roads, names, basket IDs, courier IDs, arbitrary prompts and memory bodies are excluded. This gateway has no database, queue, browser or arbitrary tool interface. A request is bounded to 8192 serialized bytes, the client waits 30 seconds, Vertex has a 5 second token-count timeout and 15 second generation timeout, output including reported reasoning is limited to 256 tokens, and responses are size/schema checked. Retries are not automatic. Cloud Run scales to zero and at most one instance, with four concurrent requests. These are usage bounds, not a guaranteed monetary cap; model pricing and other project usage can create charges. Choose a model with known price/context limits and use the local durable budget as the admission gate.

## Manual shutdown (the stop command runs these phases)

Routine shutdown uses **apply**, not `terraform destroy`. Keep the project and
its state. In `infra/gcp-ai`, run these two phases in order, reviewing each plan:

```bash
terraform plan -var='enable_billing=true' -var='enable_runtime=false' -var='enable_gateway=false' -out=stop-runtime.tfplan
terraform apply stop-runtime.tfplan
terraform plan -var='enable_billing=false' -var='enable_runtime=false' -var='enable_gateway=false' -out=park.tfplan
terraform apply park.tfplan
```

Phase one deletes Cloud Run (including revisions), its service-specific invocation
binding, and repository/images. The free IAM foundation stays in state: both
service accounts, the prediction-only custom role, its runtime binding, and
operator impersonation permissions on the caller.
Billing must stay linked until deletion finishes: Artifact Registry management
requests can fail with billing disabled. Phase two unlinks billing. For manual operation, save
all three flags as false in the private override so the next ordinary plan stays
parked. The command writes its own `zz-demo.auto.tfvars.json` after successful apply. Clear the obsolete gateway image digest; rebuild and push it
when starting another session. Do not unlink billing first or apply all three
false directly from an active deployment.

API registrations can remain enabled without provisioned runtime resources;
`disable_on_destroy=false` avoids service dependency failures. A parked state
tracks the protected project, six API registrations and five IAM resources (12
resources total). Verify a no-change plan, `ACTIVE` project,
`billingEnabled: false`, and absence of Cloud Run services. Confirm repository
removal during phase one; once billing is disabled its list API may be unavailable.
Recreate the local app with base `compose.yaml` to remove cloud credentials and
endpoint settings. Historical charges and retained platform audit records are
not erased. This switch controls this root's resources, not resources manually
created elsewhere or unrelated projects.

Full project deletion requires a separate explicit decision and deliberate removal
of both protection settings. An ordinary destroy plan must fail on `prevent_destroy`.

[Google restoration and billing behavior](https://docs.cloud.google.com/resource-manager/docs/delete-restore-projects)
and [Terraform project deletion protection](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/google/7.14.1/docs/resources/google_project).

## Verification and sources

The adapter tests use mocked transport and never contact GCP. `terraform fmt`, provider initialization and `terraform validate` pass. Live deployment evidence and initial/final eval outcomes are recorded in [verification](GCP-VERIFICATION.md).

Official references: [Cloud Run service identity](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/configuring/services/service-identity), [authenticated invocation and ID tokens](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/authenticating/service-to-service), [Vertex REST generation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/start/quickstart), [Vertex response and token metadata](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/reference/rest/v1/GenerateContentResponse), [Terraform project deletion policy](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/google/latest/docs/resources/google_project), [Terraform Cloud Run deletion protection](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/google/latest/docs/resources/cloud_run_v2_service).

## Local Docker opt-in

The regular `compose.yaml` never mounts cloud credentials. For the explicit GCP
option, set `DELIVERY_GCP_AI_ENDPOINT`, `DELIVERY_GCP_AI_CALLER_SERVICE_ACCOUNT`,
and `GCP_ADC_DIRECTORY` (the local directory containing the ADC file created by
`gcloud auth application-default login`). Then run
`docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.gcp-ai.yaml up -d --build app`.
The override mounts that directory read-only; never copy ADC into the repository
or image. Select GCP AI recovery judge in Configure and save for the next run.
Each cloud-enabled session freezes its gateway origin. Reverting to local rules
affects new sessions and makes no inference requests. The UI switch does not
apply or destroy Terraform. Use the isolated Terraform root for lifecycle changes.


## Guided redeployment and inspection

Keep the demo local until an explicit cloud session is wanted. Reuse the restored
project ID and original standalone state. The original service accounts and custom

Routine shutdown now retains these identities, so no repeated recovery is needed.

immutable digest. Follow the bootstrap steps above and refresh the local compose

For the next guided session, inspect these in order:

# GCP components: exact implementation and ownership

Source review: 2026-10-28. These are the resources and call paths defined by this
repository. No cloud resources were started or queried for this documentation
change. Last live lifecycle evidence is dated 2026-10-25 in
[GCP verification](GCP-VERIFICATION.md): the dedicated project was ACTIVE, billing
disabled and billable demo runtime removed. Run the documented status command to
check a later session; do not treat a source review as a fresh cloud inventory.

## Architecture as built

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph Local[Local Docker environment]
        UI[Operator UI and trusted controller]
        Agents[Scoped Python role workers]
        DB[(Postgres: domain state, queue, memory, budgets, audit)]
        Caller[CloudJudge client and caller ID token]
        UI --> Agents
        Agents <--> DB
        Agents -->|Optional judge policy only| Caller
    end
    subgraph GCP[Dedicated Terraform-owned GCP project]
        IAM[Cloud Run IAM invocation check]
        Gateway[Cloud Run judgement service]
        Vertex[Google publisher model through Vertex REST]
        Registry[Artifact Registry: pinned gateway image]
        Logs[Platform logs and structured gateway stdout]
        IAM --> Gateway
        Registry -.-> Gateway
        Gateway -->|Runtime service account ADC| Vertex
        Gateway --> Logs
    end
    Caller -->|HTTPS and audience-bound ID token| IAM
    Gateway -->|Schema-validated verdict and usage| Caller
```

Inventory, restaurants, dispatch, courier motion, canonical memory and the durable
queue run locally. Redis is a local baseline support service; it is not the
authoritative agent transport. There is no Cloud SQL, Pub/Sub, GKE, managed agent
runtime, managed Memory Bank or ADK deployment in this Terraform root.

## Terraform resource inventory

[main.tf](../infra/gcp-ai/main.tf) is the only cloud infrastructure root for this
demo. It requires Terraform 1.6+ and Google provider `~> 7.0`; the committed provider
lock file resolves an exact selected build. State is local to this root and ignored
by Git. Scrapmarket's project, backend and credentials are not imported or reused.

| Terraform address | Purpose and actual configuration | Retained when parked? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `google_project.ai` | Dedicated project; no default network; application labels; `deletion_policy=PREVENT` and `prevent_destroy=true` | Yes |
| `google_project_service.api["run.googleapis.com"]` | Cloud Run administration API | Yes |
| `google_project_service.api["artifactregistry.googleapis.com"]` | Container repository API | Yes |
| `google_project_service.api["aiplatform.googleapis.com"]` | Google model inference/token-counting API | Yes |
| `google_project_service.api["iam.googleapis.com"]` | Service-account/role administration | Yes |
| `google_project_service.api["iamcredentials.googleapis.com"]` | Short-lived impersonated credentials | Yes |
| `google_project_service.api["cloudresourcemanager.googleapis.com"]` | Project lifecycle/metadata | Yes |
| `google_service_account.judge[0]` | `judgement-runtime`, attached to the Cloud Run service | Yes |
| `google_project_iam_custom_role.judge_predict[0]` | `boundedJudgePredict`: only `aiplatform.endpoints.predict` | Yes |
| `google_project_iam_member.vertex[0]` | Grants that custom prediction role to the runtime account | Yes |
| `google_service_account.caller[0]` | `judgement-caller`, separate invocation identity | Yes |
| `google_service_account_iam_binding.caller_tokens[0]` | Explicit operator/service principals may impersonate the caller via `roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator` | Yes |
| `google_artifact_registry_repository.images[0]` | Regional Docker repository `judgement`; image storage can cost money | No |
| `google_cloud_run_v2_service.judge[0]` | Regional stateless `judgement` endpoint | No |
| `google_cloud_run_v2_service_iam_binding.invoker[0]` | Only the caller service account receives this service's `roles/run.invoker` binding | No |

That is **12 retained foundation resources**, plus **3 runtime resources** when
fully enabled. Provider-managed service agents, service revisions and platform
audit records are not independent resources declared in this root. The project
IAM binding is additive; the service-account/service bindings are authoritative
for their respective roles. Shared-project IAM must not be managed accidentally.

The invoker member validation accepts explicit user/service-account principals,
not public principals. The current Cloud Run setting is nevertheless
`INGRESS_TRAFFIC_ALL`: the HTTPS endpoint is network-reachable, with IAM protecting
invocation. **Authenticated invocation is not private network ingress.** There is
no VPC, IAP front end, Agent Gateway or Model Armor resource in the deployed module.

## Service sizing, build and model configuration

| Setting | Current code |
| --- | --- |
| Container | Python 3.12 slim, locked Python dependencies, FastAPI/Uvicorn, UID/GID 65532 |
| Contents | Gateway source, meal-snapshot validator and synthetic `data/meal-snapshot.json`; no database exports or agent credentials |
| Build | Local Docker `linux/amd64` build; no Cloud Build job or staging bucket |
| Image | Local push to Artifact Registry; lifecycle helper verifies a single repository digest and deploys the immutable `@sha256` reference |
| CPU / memory | 1 vCPU / 512 MiB; request-based CPU allocation, startup boost off |
| Scaling | Service and template minimum 0, maximum 1; concurrency 4 |
| Request timeout | Cloud Run 35 seconds; local caller 30 seconds |
| Gateway input/output | Strict Pydantic objects; 8,192-byte assembled request bound; 256 maximum output tokens; bounded response reads |
| Vertex transport | REST `:countTokens` followed by `:generateContent`, authenticated using runtime ADC |
| Token/request timing | Token count timeout 5 seconds, generation request timeout 15 seconds; successful response usage is checked |
| Thinking / output | `MINIMAL`, JSON MIME type, two-decision response schema; these settings require a compatible model |
| Runtime environment | `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT`, `VERTEX_REGION`, `VERTEX_MODEL` |

Sources are [Dockerfile](../infra/gcp-ai/Dockerfile),
[gateway.py](../infra/gcp-ai/gateway.py),
[variables.tf](../infra/gcp-ai/variables.tf) and
[gcp_demo.py](../scripts/gcp_demo.py). Terraform requires explicit region, model
location and model identifier; this documentation does not read private variable
files. Historically verified values were Cloud Run `europe-west1`, Vertex
`global`, and `gemini-3.5-flash-lite`. That deployment is **not** an EU-only
inference processing claim. Returned model version and gateway revision are more
useful experiment provenance than a model-family label alone.

Zero minimum instances is a demo cost/latency choice, not an availability SLO or
guarantee of no storage/logging/inference charges. Configured maximum instances
and concurrency constrain capacity, not total spend. See
[Cloud Run billing behavior](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/configuring/billing-settings).

## Authentication, step by step

1. An explicitly cloud-enabled local run freezes its gateway origin. Base Compose
   does not mount cloud credentials. The opt-in
   [Compose override](../compose.gcp-ai.yaml) mounts the operator's ADC directory
   read-only; it is never copied into an image or Git.
2. `identity_token` in [cloud_ai.py](../src/delivery/cloud_ai.py) uses ADC to
   impersonate `judgement-caller`, obtaining an ID token whose audience is the
   gateway service origin. The client accepts only a Cloud Run HTTPS origin.
3. Cloud Run checks that token and its service-level invocation policy before
   FastAPI handles `/judge`. The application relies on this platform authentication;
   it does not independently validate arbitrary JWTs or enforce per-tenant quotas.
4. Cloud Run executes as `judgement-runtime`. Runtime ADC provides OAuth access
   to the Google publisher model through its prediction-only custom role. No
   downloaded service-account key or model API key is needed.
5. The cloud runtime has no simulation database connection or business action
   tools. It returns a verdict; local SQL still decides whether any retry is legal.

The custom role is prediction-only at **project** scope, not an IAM allowlist for
one model ID. The configured model is an application-controlled selection. The
caller impersonation role can mint more than ID tokens; a client deployment should
test whether its actual flow can use a narrower grant. Neither current account is
a managed Agent Identity with runtime-bound agent credentials.

This follows the distinction between caller ID tokens and runtime service identity
in Google's [authenticated invocation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/authenticating/service-to-service)
and [service identity](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/configuring/services/service-identity)
guides. Local ADC is a development credential flow. Enterprise CI should use
restricted Workload Identity Federation, not a copied user ADC file.

## Exactly what reaches the model

`sanitized_request` permits finite numeric values for `attempt`, `retry_limit`,
`deadline_sim`, `sim_time` and optional `cost_eur`; a candidate contains only
`estimated_seconds`, `remaining_seconds` and `route_nodes`. It sends the number
of recalled entries, capped at 100, **not their bodies**. Customer names, order IDs,
courier IDs, route coordinates, local SOUL and private Bakiano rows are omitted.

The gateway adds its packaged seven-meal, seventeen-ingredient, three-fictional-
market snapshot. Its fixed prompt permits only `approve_retry` or `deny_retry`
with a short reason; it exposes no tools. Snapshot and prompt versions are logged.
This is read-only reference for pizza, kebab, hamburgers, steak frites, sushi, soups
and salads; the judge does not procure ingredients or substitute a meal.

Before inference, deterministic preflight denies absent/invalid numeric facts,
missing candidates, exhausted retries and infeasible deadlines/route duration.
The 6,000-second route threshold is a simulation step/duration bound, **not a GCP
monetary budget**. A JSON-conforming answer is still subject to local feasibility
and custody checks. Authentication, transport or validation failure denies the
AI-enabled retry. No silent switch to local approval is made within that run.

The configured cumulative allowance is six calls/50,688 tokens per run. Each
newly dispatched request reserves 8,448 tokens; saved-result replay does not reserve
another call. The whole allowance is not
reserved upfront. This does not enforce a project-wide currency budget,
block another authorized direct caller, or guarantee exactly-once model billing.
The local judge adapter now commits a request and dispatch marker, closes its
database connection for remote I/O, saves the result and applies it in a fresh
fenced transaction. Reclaimed events reuse completed results; uncertain abandoned
invocations fail closed without automatic resend. This changes local orchestration,
not the deployed Terraform resource inventory. See [durable inference](DURABLE-INFERENCE.md).

## Observability and its current limits

Gateway structured stdout records event class, decision, prompt version, snapshot
hash, Cloud Run revision and, for actual model answers, model version, token usage
and elapsed milliseconds. Preflight denials record zero model tokens. Local model
audit records attach provider/verdict/usage/error class to the event attempt.

Platform request/audit logging and gateway stdout are available, but Terraform does
not configure custom log retention, dashboards, alert policies, Cloud Trace spans
or OpenTelemetry export. There is no complete distributed trace from the local
order through Cloud Run/Vertex: correlation IDs are deliberately excluded from the
model body, and a separate sanitized tracing propagation channel remains to be
added. Do not describe the local event inspector as deployed Cloud Trace or as
access to a model's private reasoning.

## Start, inspect and park

These are operational commands, **not steps required to read this documentation**:

```bash
make gcp-start
make gcp-status
make gcp-stop
```

`start` verifies prerequisites, links billing with runtime enabled/gateway disabled,
builds/pushes the image, then deploys the gateway and reconnects the local app.
It enables the UI option but does not select it or initiate inference. `status`
reads project/billing/service/state information and never links billing merely to
inspect Artifact Registry. That check is reported unavailable when billing is off.

`stop` first attempts to restore base local Compose, then removes the service,
invoker binding and image repository **while billing is still linked**. A second
Terraform apply unlinks billing. Project, APIs and IAM identities remain. The helper
validates saved plans against phase-specific resource/project allowlists and uses
a local lifecycle lock. Shutdown failure is explicit; it is not reported as parked.

Ordinary `terraform destroy` is intentionally blocked by project protection.
This implements the later requirement to preserve project/IAM between sessions.
Full project erasure is a separate reviewed lifecycle change, not the daily stop
command. Prior invoices, delayed usage reporting and retained platform audit
records are not erased. The helper controls this root's resources, not arbitrary
resources created manually or in another project.

Cloud SQL, remote Terraform state buckets, secrets, managed memory, traces and any
future paid service must have an explicit owner, Terraform coverage and stop/data-
retention policy before adoption. A production retention requirement can introduce
an intentional cost floor; it must never be advertised as a free parked demo.
See [the complete operations runbook](GCP-AI.md).

## Deployment and data boundary

A new dedicated project, `mds-ai-judge-261024-c7b4`, was provisioned from
`infra/gcp-ai` using the operator-selected billing account. No Scrapmarket project,
Terraform state or resources were modified. Cloud Run is in `europe-west1`;
Vertex uses the explicitly selected `global` endpoint. This is not an EU-only
inference residency claim. Only synthetic data was sent.

Ready revision: `judgement-00002-92k`. Immutable image:
`sha256:71834c8a002596752dd560c957ae75dae86041c582467805b6f3473292bbdd15`.
Model: `gemini-3.5-flash-lite`, minimal thinking. Prompt version:
`recovery-v2-seven-meals`. Snapshot SHA-256:
`5be219156af219ac97f41dd53e96024107e5eb68457da14cd3015c1c8d914f19`.
The snapshot contains seven meals, 17 ingredients and three fictional supermarkets.
It is reviewed read-only context; the judge does not perform procurement.

## Eval findings and repair

The initial live run passed 4/6 cases: five valid model responses, one provider
error, and one unsafe model approval when required facts were missing. The SQL
executor already retained independent policy enforcement. We preserved this result
rather than treating deployment success as model correctness.

We added a deterministic gateway preflight for missing facts, absent candidates,
retry exhaustion, deadline and route-cost constraints. Final system results:
6/6 cases passed, zero provider errors and zero hard-policy violations. This was
**one model decision and five policy-gate denials**, not six LLM decisions.
Six toy cases do not establish general model quality, a production SLO, or business
uplift over rules. See the [initial](evidence/gcp-judge-initial.json) and
[guarded](evidence/gcp-judge-guarded.json) receipts.

The guarded eval used 2,150 input and 35 output tokens. At the documented global
rates of $0.30 / $2.50 per million input/output tokens, its successful model usage
is estimated at $0.0007325. This excludes failed/unreported generations, earlier
probes, Cloud Run, storage, logging, taxes and currency conversion. It is not an
invoice or project-wide cost cap. [Google pricing](https://cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/generative-ai/pricing).

## End-to-end UI switch

The former live-cloud script (retired with the Delivery grid UI) configured
seed 71, 15 minutes of demand, four orders/hour, traffic 1, dropout intensity 0.4,
and three couriers based at one shop. The seed naturally withdraws bike-1 at
simulated second 694; no incident was injected after session creation.

The GCP-mode run `fe8fbad6-103f-42ff-8fd1-1e12e384cb02` recorded one actual model
approval, one durable 8,448-token reservation and no fallback. The paired local-mode
run `95057578-594a-42ed-b2e1-2862104f139e` recorded zero model calls. All stock,
assignment, custody, retry-approval and budget invariants passed; browser errors
were empty. [UI verification receipt](evidence/gcp-switch-verification.json).

Unauthenticated invocation returned 403; authenticated malformed input returned
422. Neither negative check invokes the model. The caller can invoke only this
service; the runtime custom role contains only `aiplatform.endpoints.predict`.
No service-account keys were created. [Negative checks](evidence/gcp-negative-checks.json).

## Teardown coverage

A reviewed `terraform plan -destroy` contains exactly 15 deletions, covering the
service and revisions, invocation IAM, custom role and prediction binding, both
service accounts, repository/images, enabled-service resources, and the dedicated
project. Every planned resource belongs to this project. Project deletion owns
implicit service agents and other platform-created project children. No shared
billing account or operator identity is deleted.

**Teardown executed on 2026-10-25:** Terraform reported 15 destroyed resources;
`terraform state list` is empty. Google reports the dedicated project as
`DELETE_REQUESTED`, so final project erasure remains asynchronous and subject to
platform retention. The local app is healthy with `local: true`, `gcp_ai: false`
and the cloud credential override removed. Scrapmarket was not touched.
[Actual teardown receipt](evidence/gcp-teardown-result.json).
The earlier [plan receipt](evidence/gcp-teardown-plan.json) records the pre-execution check.

## Enterprise interpretation

The useful interview evidence is controlled rollout and a documented failure/repair,
not a claim that an LLM is necessary for numeric feasibility. Keep local rules as the
baseline and default. Before exposing more users, add gateway-wide admission budgets,
held-out business evals, stronger release automation, recovery SLOs and finance
reconciliation. [Architecture and tradeoffs](ENTERPRISE-GCP.md).


## Restored persistent project (2026-10-25)

After the completed historical teardown above, the user requested keeping the
project between demos. The dedicated project was restored, imported into the
same Terraform root, and protected against deletion. Its current lifecycle is
`ACTIVE`, billing is disabled, and state contains only `google_project.ai`.

Six mocked Terraform runs cover parked defaults, active deployment, deleting

# Run evidence in BigQuery

The simulation stays local. Analytics is an explicit export of existing evidence: it never starts a run, asks a model a question, changes inference admission limits, or executes a BigQuery query. The default workflow writes inspectable local files and needs no Google credentials. Terraform defaults to `enable_bigquery=false` and creates no analytics storage or service account.

## Prepare and inspect a free bundle

From an installed development environment, use an existing offline receipt:

```bash
python3 scripts/export_bigquery.py prepare \
  --receipt artifacts/adk-restaurants-demo.json \
  --output artifacts/bigquery/demo
```

The exporter accepts both native receipt formats:

- Baseline simulation: `artifacts/run-<run-id>.json`, with a nested `run` object containing `id`, timezone-qualified `created_at`, `status`, and model accounting, plus top-level `metrics`. Delivery measurements include orders, delivered/on-time counts, on-time percentage, active/unserved work, delivery cost and cost per delivery.
- ADK comparisons: a top-level timezone-qualified `created_at`, a `profiles` or `arms` list, and per-run `run` UUID, `metrics`, and boolean `invariants` or `outcome_checks`. This includes `artifacts/adk-route-comparison.json` and `artifacts/adk-live-comparison.json`. Generate a fresh offline receipt with `make demo-adk` if needed.

Use either format with the same `prepare --receipt ... --output ...` command. Missing invariant or replay evidence stays unmeasured.

The output contains:

| File | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `run_receipts.ndjson` | Run ID, receipt/source hashes, run and export timestamps, profile/scenario/variant, recorded status, replay result, passed/total checks, and cost evidence. |
| `run_kpis.ndjson` | Allowlisted numeric delivery, queue, ADK, search, and router measurements, one row per metric. |
| `manifest.json` | SHA-256, row count and byte count for both tables. |

Raw prompts, transcripts, provider responses, configuration, credentials, and free-form error text are excluded. Unknown metrics remain absent; incomplete cost accounting remains null. `usage_cost_usd` uses known usage at the receipt's frozen tariffs only when every call is accounted for. It is not a billing invoice. `reserved_cost_usd` remains a separate admission amount; explicit zero-paid-call receipts can report zero cost. A missing status is `recorded`, never inferred to be completed.

Baseline `llm_cost_usd`, `llm_calls`, tokens and reservations are retained as numeric KPIs. Their aggregate values do not prove every admitted model call returned usage. Consequently, a baseline receipt with model calls retains null `usage_cost_usd` even if its observed cost is zero. Only an explicit zero call count proves zero model usage for that format; missing call counts do not. The reserved amount remains separately visible.

Preparation refuses to overwrite a bundle. Keep the bundle unchanged for retries. Source files are capped at 32 MiB; each export is capped at 100 runs and 1 MiB. All generated files belong under ignored `artifacts/`.

## Optional cloud setup

This is a separate, opt-in demo alongside the existing GCP judge lifecycle. No cloud deployment or upload runs in CI. Use the dedicated project already configured in the ignored Terraform variables, and review the plan before applying:

```bash
terraform -chdir=infra/gcp-ai plan \
  -var=enable_bigquery=true -var=enable_billing=true \
  -out=analytics-enable.tfplan
terraform -chdir=infra/gcp-ai apply analytics-enable.tfplan
terraform -chdir=infra/gcp-ai output bigquery_analytics
```

The plan provisions an EU dataset by default, two tables partitioned by `exported_at` and clustered by run/hash, and the `run_dashboard` GoogleSQL view. Both tables require a partition filter and expire partitions after seven days. Change `bigquery_location` before creating the dataset if required; it is independent of the Vertex region. Retention and the upload size cap bound this demonstration's data footprint; they are not a total billing cap. Storage and dashboard queries can incur charges while enabled.

The keyless `delivery-analytics` service account has a custom dataset-scoped role limited to table create/get/update/updateData and a project role containing only jobs.create. It cannot read table data, delete tables, administer IAM, or invoke Vertex. The uploader sets `CREATE_NEVER`: table creation belongs to Terraform. Only the explicit `invoker_members` can impersonate this identity. No service-account keys are created. Keep dashboard reader access separate from this write-only loader.

## Upload only the reviewed bundle

Use an installed Python environment with the project dependencies and Application Default Credentials. Set the project ID from the Terraform output; no project ID or credentials are committed:

```bash
export ANALYTICS_PROJECT='your-dedicated-project'
export DELIVERY_BIGQUERY_ENABLED=1
python3 scripts/export_bigquery.py upload \
  --bundle artifacts/bigquery/demo \
  --project "$ANALYTICS_PROJECT" \
  --service-account "delivery-analytics@$ANALYTICS_PROJECT.iam.gserviceaccount.com" \
  --dataset delivery_analytics --location EU \
  --confirm-upload
unset DELIVERY_BIGQUERY_ENABLED
```

Both the environment opt-in and `--confirm-upload` are required before credentials are loaded. The bundle is checked against its manifest before either table is uploaded. Loads append to existing tables, reject unknown columns/bad records, and use stable job IDs derived from the exact destination and frozen bytes. Retrying the same bundle recovers an existing load job after a conflict. The two table loads are independent: after a partial failure, repeat the same upload command. Do not prepare another bundle as a retry. BigQuery job deduplication is bounded by its retained job history; the dashboard additionally selects the latest export per run and collapses duplicate metric rows. Old exports expire with their partitions.

## Looker Studio dashboard

Connect Looker Studio's BigQuery connector to the Terraform output `dashboard_view` using a separate reader identity with the necessary dataset read and project job permissions. The view is ready to select as a table, so no custom SQL is needed in Looker Studio.

Suggested controls are `run_date`, `profile`, `scenario`, and `variant`. Add delivery rate, queue events, dead letters, replay result, and evaluation pass rate; compare measured usage cost with reserved cost in separate series. `evaluation_pass_rate` is the run receipt's boolean-check pass rate, not the entire repository's scenario evaluation score. Missing denominators and missing usage stay null. Both source tables are filtered to the last seven export days. Choose bounded refresh intervals and inspect BigQuery billing before making a dashboard public; this feature does not publish one automatically.

The same view supports baseline receipts: `delivery_rate` divides delivered orders by ADK `scheduled_calls` when present, otherwise baseline `orders`. It also exposes baseline `on_time`, `on_time_pct`, `delivery_cost_eur`, `cost_per_delivery_eur`, `active`, `unserved`, `pending`, and `overdue` columns. `delivery_rate` is a fraction (0–1); the simulator's `on_time_pct` is already a percentage (0–100). A zero denominator remains null, and baseline receipts without outcome checks retain a null evaluation pass rate.

## Park analytics

Stop uploads by clearing `DELIVERY_BIGQUERY_ENABLED`. To return to no analytics storage, explicitly remove this disposable dataset while billing is still linked:

`gcp_demo.py status` lists `analytics_in_state` and `telemetry_in_state`; retained optional components are never reported as fully parked. `stop` checks these resources before restarting the app or changing cloud resources and gives cleanup instructions if any remain. Once cleanup is complete, its parking plans explicitly keep both optional flags false so stale opt-in settings cannot recreate them.

```bash
unset DELIVERY_BIGQUERY_ENABLED
terraform -chdir=infra/gcp-ai plan \
  -var=enable_bigquery=false -var=enable_billing=true \
  -out=analytics-disable.tfplan
terraform -chdir=infra/gcp-ai apply analytics-disable.tfplan
python3 scripts/gcp_demo.py stop
```

Review the removal plan: it deletes the analytics tables and view. Original local receipts remain available. The dataset refuses to delete unexpected, unmanaged contents. Preserve `enable_bigquery=true` on intervening Terraform commands while the analytics demo is active; command-line flags are not persisted. Remove analytics explicitly before the existing judge stop command unlinks billing. The enabled BigQuery API registration can remain after storage and IAM are removed and does not itself store run data.

## Verification and API references

`tests/test_bigquery_export.py` covers local-only preparation, allowlisting, incomplete accounting, strict opt-in, artifact tampering, stable load IDs, SDK load configuration and recovery, and payload limits. `infra/gcp-ai/tests/bigquery.tftest.hcl` uses the mocked Google provider to check parked defaults, billing opt-in, retention, scoped permissions and the view. These checks make no paid calls. The cloud path has not been live-uploaded as part of this change.

Inspect the [exporter](../src/delivery/bigquery_export.py), [command](../scripts/export_bigquery.py), [unit tests](../tests/test_bigquery_export.py), [Terraform resources](../infra/gcp-ai/bigquery.tf), [infrastructure tests](../infra/gcp-ai/tests/bigquery.tftest.hcl), and [dashboard SQL view](../infra/gcp-ai/sql/run_dashboard.sql).

Official documentation checked on 2026-10-29:

- [Import a local file](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/samples/bigquery-load-from-file) and [Python Client 3.46.2](https://docs.cloud.google.com/python/docs/reference/bigquery/latest/google.cloud.bigquery.client.Client): binary file loads, fixed job IDs, location, and job completion.
- [Batch-loading permissions](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/batch-loading-data): table load permissions and jobs.create.
- [BigQuery IAM](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/access-control): resource-scoped grants and separation of data access from job execution.

# Google stack: demonstrate a decision and its evidence

This portfolio slice connects Google ADK, A2A, OpenTelemetry, and BigQuery to a
working delivery simulator. The core demonstration is free: PostgreSQL owns
state, queue leases, permissions, memory and budgets; scripted ADK models exercise
the real Runner; Jaeger inspects local traces. Cloud features remain separately
enabled and no paid provider is invoked in CI.

## A short technical demonstration

1. Start with `make setup` and open `/architecture`, `/agent-traces`, and `/health`.
2. Run `make demo-adk` to compare scripted restaurant behaviors with stored tool,
   outcome and usage evidence. The fixture measures contract compliance, not LLM quality.
3. Discover both [A2A agents](A2A.md). Call an existing order or complaint with
   the official client and inspect its durable event, outcome, and replay.
4. Enable [local tracing](OBSERVABILITY.md), repeat a run, and follow a trace from
   the queue producer through an agent and its tools into downstream work.
5. [Prepare a BigQuery bundle](GOOGLE-ANALYTICS.md) from the receipt. Inspect the
   allowlisted rows and SQL dashboard view without contacting Google Cloud.

This shows how a customer-facing engineer can move from a business failure
(late delivery, stock contention, courier dropout) to a bounded agent action,
an auditable result, and an operational metric.

## Google ADK customer service

The [customer adapter](../src/delivery/adk_customer.py) replaces the former direct
GenAI call with `LlmAgent`, `Runner`, and `InMemorySessionService`. It uses a strict
Advice schema, no tools or transfers, one model call, no automatic provider
retries, and a bound on the complete serialized request. The existing
[service](../src/delivery/customer_service.py) still admits work through a durable
reservation before invoking the model, reuses cached results, and falls back to
operator review after an error, exhausted budget, or disabled provider.

`LLM_PROVIDER=offline` selects the scripted customer model, which records zero
dollars but still consumes the existing call/token allowance. `disabled` remains
the default outside the explicit local A2A demonstration. Paid `gemini` and
`vertex` modes retain the original call, token and dollar ceilings. The fixed
refund policy remains outside the model; the offline source cannot authorize a
refund. Unknown usage after a provider error retains its full reservation; zero
recorded tokens in an error receipt does not prove zero provider spend.

The [customer tests](../tests/test_adk_customer.py) cover the real offline Runner,
input/schema bounds, one-call enforcement, provider configuration, durable
reservation and replay. [Original safety tests](../tests/test_safety.py) continue
to verify injection handling, the refund gate and concurrent budget admission.

## Interfaces, operations and limits

| Capability | Working path | Cloud boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ADK restaurant + customer | Real Runner, scripted model, scoped tools or structured Advice | Explicit Vertex/Gemini configuration; existing budget gates |
| A2A | Two 1.0 JSON-RPC servers, cards and real SDK client | Loopback demonstration; external tenant authentication is not implemented |
| OpenTelemetry | W3C queue propagation and local Jaeger, linked from trace inspector | Explicit collector export, trace-only service account, sampling |
| BigQuery | Local NDJSON receipts/KPIs, frozen manifest, mocked upload tests | Opt-in dataset/tables/view, bounded batch loads, scoped service account |
| Looker Studio | Dashboard-ready BigQuery SQL view and field guide | Connecting a live dashboard is an operator step; query charges are separate |

Existing inference cost caps in [cloud_ai.py](../src/delivery/cloud_ai.py) are
unchanged. Cloud Trace ingestion, BigQuery storage and dashboard queries have
separate service pricing; none are enabled by `make setup`. Infrastructure and
upload tests use mocks, never a live GCP project. Google Maps ETA comparison and
managed Agent Engine deployment remain optional future extensions.

The [public-readiness review](PUBLIC-READINESS.md) records ignored secret/state
files and the history scan. GitHub visibility remains private. The GIF in the
README is explicitly a placeholder, not claimed footage.

## Reproduce the checks

The [local verification receipt](evidence/google-stack-local.json) records 628
passing tests, Ruff, mypy over 54 modules, twelve scenarios repeated twice with
49/49 criteria passing, mocked Terraform checks, and the Jaeger/export smoke test.
It identifies the exact regression revision and distinguishes local evidence
from untested live cloud integration.

```bash
make setup
make check
make test
make eval-agents
docker compose exec -T app pytest -q tests/test_a2a_server.py tests/test_adk_customer.py tests/test_telemetry.py tests/test_bigquery_export.py
python3 scripts/check_documentation.py
```

Run suites using the shared `delivery_test` database sequentially; concurrent
suites can invalidate fixture-cleanup assertions. Terraform checks use an
isolated working directory, a mocked provider, and Terraform 1.14 or newer
(which handles protected resources during mock-test teardown). See each feature
guide for exact cloud opt-in and parking commands. No live Cloud Trace or
BigQuery deployment is claimed by these local checks.

Official API documentation checked on 2026-10-29:

- [ADK agents](https://adk.dev/agents/llm-agents/), [Gemini models](https://adk.dev/agents/models/google-gemini/), and [RunConfig](https://adk.dev/runtime/runconfig/).
- [A2A Python SDK](https://a2aproject.github.io/a2a-python/) and [server routes](https://a2a-protocol.org/latest/tutorials/python/5-start-server/).
- [Cloud Trace Python/OTel](https://docs.cloud.google.com/trace/docs/setup/python-ot).
- [BigQuery local-file loads](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/samples/bigquery-load-from-file) and [IAM permissions](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/access-control).

# Local health and evaluation evidence

Open [Health & evals](http://localhost:8010/health) from the delivery, restaurant or
inventory workspace. The category tally and recent-run pattern follows the
Scrapmarket health page; this implementation uses local files and probes, with
no Firestore, cloud deployment or model requests.

## Collect evidence

Start the stack with `make up`. Then, from Bash:

```bash
make health
```

This builds a disposable checker container, runs the full pytest suite against
`delivery_test`, runs Ruff and mypy, evaluates twelve role scenarios twice, and
evaluates the fixed recovery-judge rules baseline. It does not restart the running
app or its database/Redis dependencies.
The checker forces `LLM_PROVIDER=disabled`; its evaluation command never accepts a
cloud endpoint. It requires a configured `delivery_test` URL and also binds the
subprocesses' default database to that test database. A nonzero test/check result
makes the command fail while preserving
the available evidence. Source edits during the check also make it fail.

`make test` also records case-level test results. GitHub CI uses the same local
runner and uploads its safe JSON reports even on failure. CI artifacts are not
automatically downloaded into the local dashboard.

The checker image is Python-only. JavaScript syntax is explicitly **unavailable**
there when Node is absent; this is not counted as a pass and does not fail the
Python check command. With Node available the runner checks every first-party
`web/*.js` file. A local Bash syntax check is also available:

```bash
node --check web/health.js
```

`DOCKER` can override the Docker executable, for example `make DOCKER=docker.exe
health` in a Bash environment that needs the Windows executable.

## What the page shows

- **Test catalogue:** all collected parameter cases, explicit categories, search,
  result and integration filters. Expand a file, then a check for its description,
  source line, original case ID, duration and failing phase. Descriptions come from
  test docstrings or names; they are not generated assertions about test coverage.
- **Role scenarios:** inventory, restaurant, dispatcher and courier scorecards,
  failed-case/role filters, expandable expected/actual criteria, repetition numbers
  and bounded source event trails. `make eval-agents` runs only these scenarios.
  All 49 declared criteria are scored; a correct business refusal can be a pass.
  See [scenario contracts, scoring and reproducibility](AGENT-EVALS.md).
- **Capability regressions:** selected regressions for queue resilience, coordination,
  memory isolation, budget admission, disrupted-city scenarios and replay. Each
  card links to its cases and states its limits. These groups overlap and must
  not be added into a second test total.
- **Rules baseline:** the six fixed recovery-judge cases, with expected and actual
  decisions and local latency. The rules oracle is compared with itself. This
  checks the evaluation harness, not model quality, live latency or model cost.
- **City health:** read-only Postgres/PostGIS and Redis probes, selected-run queue
  counts, expired leases, dead letters, retries, durable run budgets and model/search
  reservations. Reservations are not actual provider usage or a monetary estimate.
  Historical failed scenarios stay visible. Business failures are distinct from
  infrastructure failure.
- **Run history:** up to 12 finished receipts, retaining their original scope,
  source and outcomes. Invalid receipts are counted as unreadable, not passed.

The page refreshes every 30 seconds while visible. The refresh button reads
existing results; it cannot execute tests or accept shell arguments. Open test
details remain expanded as results refresh. Dates use Europe/Madrid.

## Evidence boundaries

The opt-in `delivery.health_report` pytest plugin records collection and all
setup/call/teardown outcomes. A teardown failure overrides a successful call.
Skipped, expected-failure, unexpected-pass, unrun and filtered cases stay distinct.
Collection-only and interrupted runs cannot be reported as a full passing suite.
Missing evidence is unknown, with no fallback to the old headline of 307 tests.

A deterministic SHA-256 fingerprint covers source, tests, SQL, agent/config files,
web assets, scripts, fixed data including the compressed road graph, the tested
gateway source, dependency files, Dockerfile, Makefile and CI workflow. The reader
compares it with the running app's copy of those files. Host edits need a rebuilt
app to appear in that comparison. A base Git revision is supplementary metadata;
it does not replace the fingerprint for a dirty working tree.

Results older than 24 hours, changed sources, and edits during a check are marked
explicitly. Reports use atomic replacement. Failed refreshes remove current/green
claims and retain the catalogue only as historical evidence.

Reports live in ignored `artifacts/health/`. They contain test identifiers,
docstrings, statuses and timings, not captured stdout, tracebacks, failure messages,
fixture representations, environment variables, database URLs or agent memories.
Use descriptive explicit IDs for parametrized inputs rather than embedding long
payloads or credentials in case names. These files are local development receipts,
not signed attestations or a sandbox against a hostile host operator.

Role receipts additionally retain typed criterion observations and fixture-only
event metadata. Two repeated runs retain all observations: failures and omissions
cannot be erased by a later pass. The reader recomputes scores from the versioned
manifest. Source, input-configuration and business-outcome hashes make drift visible.

The read-only `/api/health/evidence` and `/api/health/runtime` endpoints are for the
trusted local operator. They use the same local-host gate as supply endpoints.
They do not grant an agent any new tool or memory access.

## Extend the dashboard

`config/health-categories.json` is the reviewed taxonomy. Give each new test file
one primary category; unmatched files appear under **Needs classification**.
Capability selectors can reference a whole test file or an exact test function;
parameter variants are included automatically. A missing selector is a visible
measurement gap. Category membership is not a percentage of requirements covered.

Live-model quality/cost, held-out scenario results, architecture comparisons,
semantic recall and long-term memory summaries remain **not measured**. Add them
with versioned fixtures, actual results, source/model versions, budget accounting
and explicit measurement scope rather than reusing the regression pass rate.

## Verification

Current role-evaluation verification (2026-10-28): 392 tests passed, Ruff and mypy
(40 source modules) passed, and the two-run seed-731 role battery matched at 12/12
cases and 49/49 criteria. All four roles scored 100% on these fixed criteria.
Browser checks covered unmeasured/running receipts, role and failed-case filters,
criterion/event repetition provenance and expanded details surviving refresh.
No console errors or horizontal page overflow; app/Postgres/Redis stayed running.
See [role evaluation receipt](evidence/agent-scenarios-local.json). The earlier
353-test dashboard baseline below is retained as historical evidence.

Verified locally on 2026-10-28: 353 tests passed, including 46 reporting/health
checks. Ruff and mypy (38 source modules) passed. The dashboard indexed 36 test
files into ten categories with no unclassified file or missing capability selector.
All six fixed offline judge cases passed, with zero model decisions or tokens.
The running app's fingerprint matched every current receipt.

Browser checks covered missing/collection evidence, source changes in history,
search and category filters, case IDs, persistent expanded inspection, capability
drill-down (15 memory cases), real historical dead-letter diagnostics, and the
explicit unmeasured model/architecture sections. Both local service probes passed;
Postgres and Redis identities/start times were unchanged by the check command.
Host JavaScript syntax passed; browser console errors and horizontal overflow were
zero at the default viewport. The Python-only checker correctly marked its missing
Node check unavailable. The [local receipt](evidence/local-health.json) records the
results and limitations.

# Local Bakiano sample and execution policy

Decision: 2026-10-23. Build and polish locally. GCP portability remains optional
future work, not a prerequisite or an always-on demo environment.

## Current frozen sample

Requested ten daily buckets: **2026-10-14 through 2026-10-23 inclusive**. Today minus
ten through today would contain eleven dates (October 13-23); ten dates including
today begin October 14.

The local private package contains **2,008 product observations** across nine
available dates, October 14-22. October 23 had no matching observations at extraction
time and remains explicitly missing. This is a frozen extraction, not a completeness
claim about later warehouse updates. No scheduled refresh or live query is required.

Sources: Gama, Central Madeirense and Plazas (supermarkets); Daka and EPA (retail).
Select at most 50 stable source listing identities per vendor across the whole
window, rather than a different random assortment every day. Individual days can
contain fewer than 50 observations per vendor. This sample is not representative
of the full assortment, market or sales. Stock, shipments and demand remain simulated.

Only vendors confirmed as USD in Bakiano's registry are selected. Preserve source
listing IDs, observed prices rounded to cents, categories/URLs where available and
missing values. The daily bucket uses warehouse ingestion date; collection timestamps
are retained in the manifest. A listing is not proof of real store availability.

Files live in ignored `data/local/bakiano/`: manifest plus one catalogue per available
day. Date entries include per-source counts and content hashes. Missing days have no
catalogue file. Never forward-fill prices or relabel old products as new observations.
The public [coverage receipt](bakiano-sample-coverage.json) contains counts only.

## Use entirely offline

The local app exposes date selection at `/lab`. Each fictional store binds to one
source catalogue; product observations remain separate from generated stock. Missing
dates cannot start runs. The manifest and chosen snapshot hash are checked before use.

```sh
docker compose up -d --build --wait
docker compose exec -T app delivery lab-demo --sample-date 2026-10-22
```

Compose mounts `data/local/` read-only and excludes it from the image build context.
The private sample is also excluded from Git. The committed synthetic fixture runs
when no private package exists. Default Compose services do not receive `.env`
credentials, remote model calls are disabled, and host settings do not implicitly
load `.env`. Explicit process environment settings remain an opt-in developer interface.

No local runtime command reads Bakiano's warehouse, starts GCP infrastructure or
refreshes the sample. Existing provider adapters are retained as optional code, not
activated by ordinary local startup.

## Optional one-time acquisition

The exporter is a separate opt-in preparation tool. It needs an authenticated
BigQuery CLI only on the machine fetching the sample, not in the application image.
It reads only selected catalogue columns for five sources and explicit date
partitions. It never modifies Bakiano tables, triggers collectors or deploys services.
The query is dry-run first and capped at 1 GiB billed bytes; LIMIT alone is not a
scan-cost control. Actual extraction processed 202,235,905 bytes, below the cap.

```sh
python scripts/export_bakiano_sample.py --project PROJECT_ID --start 2026-10-14 --end 2026-10-23
python scripts/export_bakiano_sample.py --project PROJECT_ID --start 2026-10-14 --end 2026-10-23 --execute
```

The first command only validates the query. Existing output directories are never
overwritten. For a later refresh, use `--output` with a new directory, verify its
manifest, then deliberately select/install that package. For a failed result download,
`--resume-job` retrieves a matching completed query's temporary result table without
executing the query again, while it remains available. The CLI prints its job ID
before downloading and forces UTF-8 to preserve Spanish names on Windows.

Keep extraction credentials outside datasets, prompts, event payloads and traces.
Only the root extraction process handles them; delegated code/documentation work
uses synthetic records and no private sample access.
